def-qft-photon-transverse-space.statement:
Assume Countable Choice [[def-countable-choice]]. Let
$$\mathcal H=L^2(\mathbb R^3,d^3\mathbf k;\mathbb C^3),\qquad \langle u,v\rangle_2=\int_{\mathbb R^3}\overline{u(\mathbf k)}\cdot v(\mathbf k)\,d^3\mathbf k,$$
with the second-variable-linear convention of [[def-qft-fock-and-test-spaces]]; the dot product and norm on each $\mathbb R^3$ fiber are those of [[def-euclidean-inner-product]], and Hilbert completeness follows from [[lem-l-two-with-the-integral-pairing-is-a-hilbert-space]]. For $\mathbf k\ne0$, write $n(\mathbf k)=\mathbf k/|\mathbf k|$ and
$$P_T(\mathbf k)=I_3-n(\mathbf k)n(\mathbf k)^T.$$
Assign any value at $\mathbf k=0$, which is a Lebesgue-null set. Let $M_{P_T}$ be multiplication by this measurable matrix field and define the positive transverse photon space
$$\mathcal H_T=\operatorname{Ran}M_{P_T} =\{u\in\mathcal H:\mathbf k\cdot u(\mathbf k)=0\text{ for almost every }\mathbf k\ne0\}.$$
The inner product on $\mathcal H_T$ is the restriction of that on $\mathcal H$. Each nonzero momentum fiber is the two-dimensional plane perpendicular to $\mathbf k$; no global continuous polarization frame is part of the definition.

def-qft-qed-gauge-data.statement:
Use smooth fields on Minkowski coordinate space with $x^0=ct$ and $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$. Components of $x$ are measured in metres. Fix the Dirac matrices and adjoint of [[def-qft-dirac-projections]], so $\{\gamma^a,\gamma^b\}=-2\eta^{ab}I_4$ and $\bar\psi=\psi^\dagger\beta$.

For the SI-normalization bookkeeping, let $c>0$ (m s$^{-1}$), $\hbar>0$ (J s), $\mu_0>0$ (N A$^{-2}$), a real charge parameter $q$ (C), and a mass parameter $m>0$ (kg) be symbolic inputs; put $\epsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$. In the current SI, $c$ and $h$ are defining constants while $\mu_0$ is experimentally determined; the formula below keeps $\mu_0$ symbolic and assigns it no numerical value. Use the lower-potential convention
$$A_a=(-\phi/c,\mathbf A),\qquad F_{ab}=\partial_aA_b-\partial_bA_a,$$
where $A_a$ has units T m, $\phi$ is in volts, and $\mathbf A$ is in T m. Define
$$S_0=\sqrt{\mu_0\hbar c},\qquad a_a=A_a/S_0,\qquad f_{ab}=\partial_aa_b-\partial_ba_a,$$
$$\mu=mc/\hbar,\qquad g=q\sqrt{\mu_0c/\hbar}=q/\sqrt{\epsilon_0\hbar c},\qquad D_a=\partial_a-ig a_a.$$
Thus $a_a$ and $\mu$ have units m$^{-1}$, $f_{ab}$ has units m$^{-2}$, and $g$ is dimensionless. For $\psi$ with units m$^{-3/2}$, both $-\tfrac14 f_{ab}f^{ab}$ and $\bar\psi(i\gamma^aD_a-\mu)\psi$ have units m$^{-4}$; their integral over $d^4x$ is dimensionless and represents the action divided by $\hbar$ in this normalization.

For a real smooth gauge parameter $\chi$ in webers, put $\alpha=\chi/S_0$ (dimensionless) and use
$$A'_a=A_a+\partial_a\chi,\qquad a'_a=a_a+\partial_a\alpha,\qquad \psi'=e^{ig\alpha}\psi.$$
The induced covariant derivative is $D'_a=\partial_a-ig a'_a$. These are formal mathematical conventions for the later conditional deductions. They do not adopt a measured value of $\mu_0$, identify $q$ with an electron charge, impose charge quantization, or assert that interacting continuum fields exist.

def-qft-qed-photon-energy-multiplier.statement:
Assume Countable Choice [[def-countable-choice]]. Use the transverse space $\mathcal H_T=\operatorname{Ran}M_{P_T}$ of [[def-qft-photon-transverse-space]], with $P_T(\mathbf k)=I_3-\mathbf n\mathbf n^T$ for $\mathbf k\ne0$ and any assigned value at the null point $\mathbf k=0$. In the QFT length convention, assign $\mathbf k$ units m$^{-1}$ and define the nonnegative measurable multiplier
$$ \omega(\mathbf k):=|\mathbf k|. $$
Its maximal multiplication operator on $\mathcal H_T$ is
$$ (M_\omega f)(\mathbf k):=\omega(\mathbf k)f(\mathbf k),\qquad D(M_\omega):=\{f\in\mathcal H_T:\omega f\in L^2(\mathbb R^3,d^3\mathbf k;\mathbb C^3)\}. $$
Because $\omega$ is a scalar multiplier, $\mathbf k\cdot f(\mathbf k)=0$ a.e. implies $\mathbf k\cdot(M_\omega f)(\mathbf k)=0$ a.e.; thus the displayed multiplication maps its stated domain into $\mathcal H_T$. The value $\omega(0)=0$ is immaterial to the $L^2$ operator. For $\hbar,c>0$, the corresponding one-particle energy convention is $E_1:=\hbar c M_\omega$, in joules.

def-qft-qed-physical-gauge-quantities.statement:
Use the oriented, time-oriented Minkowski model, length coordinates, metric,
and SI/natural dictionary of [[def-qft-framework-units]], with
$\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$ and $x^0=ct$. Use the gamma matrices,
Dirac adjoint, and effective Clifford metric of
[[def-qft-qed-gauge-data]]: $\gamma^0=\beta$, $\{\gamma^a,\gamma^b\}=-2\eta^{ab}I_4$,
and $\bar\psi=\psi^\dagger\beta$. Assume Countable Choice
[[def-countable-choice]] for the mathematical QFT gauge-data supplier; the
unit conversions below do not themselves spend a choice principle.

Identify the SI charge and mass symbols $q,m$ in
[[def-qft-qed-gauge-data]] with $q_{\rm SI},m_{\rm SI}$ here. Its natural
coupling $g$ is $q_{\rm n}$ below, and its inverse-length mass $\mu$ is the
same $m_{\rm SI}c/\hbar$.

Let $q_{\rm SI}\in\mathbb R$ be a selected charge parameter in coulombs and
$m_{\rm SI}>0$ a selected rest-mass parameter in kilograms. They are inputs
of the chosen model; neither is derived from Maxwell's equations. Set
$\mu=m_{\rm SI}c/\hbar$ in $\mathrm m^{-1}$ and
$q_{\rm n}=q_{\rm SI}\sqrt{\mu_0c/\hbar}$, which is dimensionless under the
framework units of [[def-qft-framework-units]]. For an electron use
$q_{\rm SI}=-e_{\rm SI}$ and
$e_{\rm n}=e_{\rm SI}\sqrt{\mu_0c/\hbar}>0$, so $q_{\rm n}=-e_{\rm n}$.
Use $\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$ with the measured current-SI
$\mu_0$ of [[def-qft-framework-units]]. These definitions therefore do not
assign an exact numerical value to $q_{\rm n}$, $e_{\rm n}$, or
$\varepsilon_0$.

In a named inertial chart, let $A^\mu_{\rm SI}=(\varphi/c,\mathbf A)$ be the
electromagnetic potential when one is supplied, with components in
$\mathrm{T\,m}$ under [[def-em-si-conventions]] and
[[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]]. Define the canonical potential and
field-strength components by

$$a^\mu:=\frac{A^\mu_{\rm SI}}{\sqrt{\mu_0\hbar c}},\qquad f^{\mu\nu}:=\frac{F^{\mu\nu}_{\rm SI}}{\sqrt{\mu_0\hbar c}}.$$

They have engineering dimensions $\mathrm m^{-1}$ and $\mathrm m^{-2}$,
respectively. With the metric-lowered potential
$A_{{\rm SI},a}=\eta_{ab}A^b_{\rm SI}$, the potential component convention is
$A_{{\rm SI},0}=-\varphi/c$ and $A_{{\rm SI},i}=A_i$. The covariant derivative
in the selected QED model is

$$D_a:=\partial_a-iq_{\rm n}a_a =\partial_a-\frac{iq_{\rm SI}}{\hbar}A_{{\rm SI},a},$$

since $q_{\rm n}a_a=q_{\rm SI}A_{{\rm SI},a}/\hbar$. Both terms in $D_a$
have unit $\mathrm m^{-1}$. If the SI gauge function $\chi$ has unit
$\mathrm{Wb}=\mathrm{T\,m^2}$, then $q_{\rm SI}\chi/\hbar$ is dimensionless;
the corresponding natural gauge function
$\lambda=\chi/\sqrt{\mu_0\hbar c}$ is dimensionless and
$q_{\rm n}\lambda=q_{\rm SI}\chi/\hbar$. These conversions apply to smooth
local gauge transformations; they assert no boundary condition, asymptotic
charge sector, or global gauge-fixing result.

If a separately specified finite regulator introduces Hamiltonian
eigenvalues, they have unit joule; this definition introduces no regulator.
The field components and units refer to the selected inertial chart, not to a
new observer congruence or a cross-framework identification.

def-qft-scalar-mass-shell.title: Scalar future mass shell, invariant measure and test restriction

def-qft-scalar-mass-shell.statement:
Assume Countable Choice [[def-countable-choice]]. Here
$\mathscr S(\mathbb R^4)$ is the Schwartz space of smooth complex functions
whose coordinate-weighted derivatives are all bounded, as defined in
[[def-schwartz-space-and-its-seminorms]].
Fix an oriented, time-oriented affine Minkowski space and an inertial coordinate
chart as in [[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]] and
[[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]]. Use coordinates
$x=(x^0,\mathbf x)$ and metric $\eta=\mathrm{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, matching the
$(-+++)$ convention of the SR suppliers. Some QFT sources use its negative
$(+---)$; the Lorentz group is unchanged, and the phase is fixed explicitly
below.
Coordinates $x$ have length units, momenta have inverse-length units, and the
Fourier phase below is dimensionless. A parameter $\mu\ge0$ has inverse-length
units and is only a mathematical shell parameter; it is not identified with a
physical rest mass. For $\mathbf k\in\mathbb R^3$, set
$$\omega_\mu(\mathbf k)=\sqrt{|\mathbf k|^2+\mu^2},\qquad p_\mu(\mathbf k)=(\omega_\mu(\mathbf k),\mathbf k).$$
The future mass shell is
$$H_\mu^+=\{(p^0,\mathbf p): (p^0)^2-|\mathbf p|^2=\mu^2,\ p^0>0\}.$$
When $\mu=0$, its apex is omitted; thus $\mathbf k\ne0$ in the massless
parameterization. The scalar shell pairing is
$$p\circ x:=p^0x^0-\mathbf p\cdot\mathbf x=-\eta(p,x).$$
Define the measure and one-particle Hilbert space by
$$d\nu_\mu(p_\mu(\mathbf k))= \frac{d^3\mathbf k}{(2\pi)^3\,2\omega_\mu(\mathbf k)},\qquad H_\mu=L^2(H_\mu^+,d\nu_\mu;\mathbb C),$$
where the omitted massless apex has measure zero. For $f\in\mathscr S(\mathbb
R^4)$ define its pointwise shell Fourier restriction by
$$K_\mu f(p)=\int_{\mathbb R^4}f(x)e^{ip\circ x}\,d^4x.$$
The Fourier convention is exactly the displayed integral, with no prefactor.
If $\widehat f(\xi^0,\boldsymbol\xi)=
\int f(x)e^{-2\pi i(x^0\xi^0+\mathbf x\cdot\boldsymbol\xi)}\,d^4x$ denotes
the standard transform in
[[cor-fourier-transform-is-a-topological-automorphism-of-schwartz-space]],
then
$$\mathcal F_+f(p^0,\mathbf p):=\int f(x)e^{i(p^0x^0-\mathbf p\cdot\mathbf x)}\,d^4x =\widehat f\!\left(-\frac{p^0}{2\pi},\frac{\mathbf p}{2\pi}\right).$$
Its inverse is
$$f(x)=(2\pi)^{-4}\int_{\mathbb R^4} \mathcal F_+f(p^0,\mathbf p)e^{-i(p^0x^0-\mathbf p\cdot\mathbf x)} \,dp^0\,d^3\mathbf p.$$
Thus this convention is a time reflection and rescaling of the cited
Schwartz automorphism and has the stated reciprocal normalization.
The proper orthochronous Lorentz group consists of linear maps preserving
$\eta$, orientation and the chosen future cone. A Poincare map is
$x\mapsto a+\Lambda x$ with $a\in\mathbb R^4$ and $\Lambda$ in that group.

This is a mathematical free scalar one-particle construction. It adopts the
chosen coordinates, measure and Fourier convention; it asserts no experimental
observation, physical mass identification or measurement outcome.

lem-qft-mass-shell-measure-invariant.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. For every $\mu\ge0$, the measure $d\nu_\mu$ of
[[def-qft-scalar-mass-shell]] is locally finite and sigma-finite on $H_\mu^+$.
For every proper orthochronous Lorentz transformation $\Lambda$ and every
nonnegative Borel function $g$ on $H_\mu^+$,
$$\int_{H_\mu^+}g(\Lambda^{-1}p)\,d\nu_\mu(p) =\int_{H_\mu^+}g(p)\,d\nu_\mu(p).$$
The claim applies off the omitted apex when $\mu=0$.

lem-qft-mass-shell-test-restriction-cont.statement:
Assume Countable Choice [[def-countable-choice]]. For every $\mu\ge0$, the
pointwise restriction
$$K_\mu f(p)=\int_{\mathbb R^4}f(x)e^{ip\circ x}\,d^4x$$
of [[def-qft-scalar-mass-shell]] maps $\mathscr S(\mathbb R^4)$ continuously
and linearly into $H_\mu$. It also annihilates the Klein–Gordon test operator:
$$K_\mu\bigl((\partial_0^2-\Delta+\mu^2)f\bigr)=0 \qquad(f\in\mathscr S(\mathbb R^4)).$$
The coordinates are the fixed length coordinates of that definition and
$\mu$ has inverse-length units.

lem-qft-photon-covariance-spectrum.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. On the future null cone write $p=(\omega,\mathbf k)$, $\omega=|\mathbf k|$, $\mathbf k\ne0$, and use the measure $d\nu=d^3\mathbf k/(2\omega)$. The fiber $p^\perp/\mathbb Cp$ has the positive quotient form of [[lem-qft-photon-null-quotient]]. For each proper orthochronous Lorentz transformation $\Lambda$, the action
$$[s(p)]\longmapsto[\Lambda s(\Lambda^{-1}p)]$$
is a unitary representation on the square-integrable quotient sections. It is strongly continuous. Under the unitary identification with $\mathcal H_T$ given by $u(\mathbf k)=s(p)/\sqrt{2\omega}$, the free translation representation has phase $e^{i(\omega a^0-\mathbf k\cdot\mathbf a)}$. Its bosonic Fock lift has joint spectrum the closed future cone
$$\overline V_+=\{(E,\mathbf P):E\ge|\mathbf P|\},$$
with the vacuum at $(0,\mathbf0)$. The energy is the nonnegative sector multiplier $\sum_{r=1}^n|\mathbf k_r|$ with the exact maximal square-integrability domain on each sector and square-summability over sectors. These are mathematical free-field representation statements.

lem-qft-photon-local-field-strength.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $A_0=0$ and let $A_i$ be the transverse potential operator-valued distribution of [[lem-qft-photon-smeared-potential]]. Set
$$F_{ab}=\partial_aA_b-\partial_bA_a,\qquad E_i=-\partial_0A_i,\qquad B_i=\epsilon_{irs}\partial_rA_s,$$
where $\epsilon_{irs}$ is the totally antisymmetric symbol with $\epsilon_{123}=1$. In the commutator formulas below, $\Delta=\sum_{r=1}^3\partial_r^2$ is the spatial Laplacian acting on $x-y$.
For a real compactly supported smooth antisymmetric test tensor $h^{ab}=-h^{ba}$, define
$$F(h)=\frac12\int_{\mathbb R^4}F_{ab}(x)h^{ab}(x)\,d^4x =-A_b(\partial_a h^{ab}).$$
The effective test is conserved, $\partial_b\partial_a h^{ab}=0$, and $F(h)$ is unchanged by $A_b\mapsto A_b+\partial_b\lambda$ for smooth $\lambda$. Its one-particle coefficient $g_h$ is the vector $g_j$ of [[lem-qft-photon-smeared-potential]] for $j_i=-\partial_a h^{ai}$, so $F(h)=a(g_h)+a^\dagger(g_h)$ on $\mathcal D_{\rm fin}$.

Let $C_0=-i\Delta_0$, where $\Delta_0$ is the massless scalar causal commutator of [[lem-qft-scalar-causal-commutator]]. As distributions in $x-y$,
$$[E_i(x),E_j(y)]=[B_i(x),B_j(y)] =(-\delta_{ij}\Delta+\partial_i\partial_j)C_0(x-y),$$
$$[E_i(x),B_j(y)]=\epsilon_{jri}\partial_0\partial_rC_0(x-y).$$
Every right-hand side has support in the closed causal cone. Hence compactly supported tests with spacelike-separated supports give commuting field-strength operators on $\mathcal D_{\rm fin}$. The quotient representation of [[lem-qft-photon-covariance-spectrum]] makes these smeared field strengths Lorentz covariant: their on-shell coefficient depends on a polarization class only through $p_a\epsilon_b-p_b\epsilon_a$. These conclusions concern gauge-invariant free observables and do not assert locality of the Coulomb potential.

lem-qft-photon-local-weyl-observables.title: Bounded local photon Weyl observable algebra

references.title: David Tong, Quantum Field Theory, Chapter 6, §§6.2.1–6.4

lem-qft-photon-local-weyl-observables.statement:
Assume Countable Choice and let $g_h\in\mathcal H_T$ be the one-particle vector for a real compactly supported antisymmetric test $h$ from [[lem-qft-photon-local-field-strength]]. The space $\mathcal H_T$ is separable: it is the range of the bounded projection $P_T$ on the separable space $L^2(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb C^3)$. Define
$$W_O(h)=W_{\rm Segal}(\sqrt2\,g_h),$$
where $W_{\rm Segal}$ is the Weyl unitary of [[lem-qft-segal-weyl-domain]]. It is bounded and unitary, and its one-parameter group has the self-adjoint field-strength closure as generator. For every open spacetime region $O$, let $\mathcal A(O)$ be the norm-closed unital $*$-algebra generated by $W_O(h)$ for tests supported in $O$; equivalently its bounded real and imaginary parts are included as observables. If $O_1,O_2$ are spacelike separated, then $\mathcal A(O_1)$ and $\mathcal A(O_2)$ commute.

lem-qft-photon-no-global-polarization-fr.title: No global continuous real polarization frame

lem-qft-photon-no-global-polarization-fr.statement: Assume Countable Choice. For $n\in S^2\subset\mathbb R^3$, let $E_n=n^\perp=\operatorname{Ran}(I-nn^T)$ be the real transverse plane. There do not exist continuous maps $e_1,e_2:S^2\to\mathbb R^3$ such that, for every $n$, $(e_1(n),e_2(n))$ is an orthonormal basis of $E_n$. A continuous real orthonormal polarization frame would in particular give a continuous nowhere-zero tangent vector field on $S^2$.

lem-qft-photon-null-quotient.statement:
Assume Countable Choice and use $\mathcal H_T$ from [[def-qft-photon-transverse-space]]. On $\mathcal K=L^2(\mathbb R^3,d^3\mathbf k;\mathbb C^4)$ define
$$[\epsilon,\delta]_\eta=\int_{\mathbb R^3}\epsilon(\mathbf k)^\dagger\eta\,\delta(\mathbf k)\,d^3\mathbf k,\qquad \eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1).$$
For $\mathbf k\ne0$, let $n=\mathbf k/|\mathbf k|$ and set
$$\mathcal K_0=\{\epsilon\in\mathcal K:-\epsilon^0+n\cdot\boldsymbol\epsilon=0\text{ a.e.}\},\qquad T\epsilon=\boldsymbol\epsilon-n\epsilon^0.$$
Then $\mathcal K_0$ is closed, $T:\mathcal K_0\to\mathcal H_T$ is bounded and onto, and
$$[\epsilon,\delta]_\eta=\langle T\epsilon,T\delta\rangle_2\quad(\epsilon,\delta\in\mathcal K_0).$$
Its radical (the vectors pairing to zero with all of $\mathcal K_0$) is
$$\mathcal N=\ker T=\{b(\mathbf k)(1,n(\mathbf k)):b\in L^2(\mathbb R^3)\}.$$
Consequently $\mathcal K_0/\mathcal N$ with the induced form is a positive Hilbert space isometric to $\mathcal H_T$. The form on the four-component auxiliary space is indefinite; only the subsidiary quotient is the positive physical one-particle space.

lem-qft-photon-smeared-potential.title: Smeared Coulomb photon operator distribution

references.title: David Tong, Quantum Field Theory, Chapter 6, §§6.2.1–6.2.2
references.locator: Complete author-hosted HTML chapter 6; transverse mode expansion and Coulomb-gauge photon field.

references.title: Mark Srednicki, Quantum Field Theory, author-hosted 2006 book draft, §§54–56
references.locator: Complete 616-page book draft; canonical transverse photon modes and Coulomb gauge.

lem-qft-photon-smeared-potential.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $j=(j_1,j_2,j_3)\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^4;\mathbb R^3)$ and use $\mathcal H_T$ and $P_T$ from [[def-qft-photon-transverse-space]]. For $\omega=|\mathbf k|$ and $\mathbf k\ne0$, define
$$g_j(\mathbf k)=\frac{1}{(2\pi)^{3/2}(2\omega)^{1/2}}\, P_T(\mathbf k)\int_{\mathbb R^4}j(x)e^{i\omega x^0-i\mathbf k\cdot\mathbf x}\,d^4x.$$
Then $g_j\in\mathcal H_T$. On the finite-particle domain $\mathcal D_{\rm fin}$ of the bosonic Fock space $\mathcal F_s(\mathcal H_T)$, the smeared transverse potential is
$$A_T(j)=a(g_j)+a^\dagger(g_j).$$
Its matrix elements are continuous in the test-function topology; it is an operator-valued distribution and does not assign a pointwise operator to $A_i(x)$. With $E_i=-\partial_0A_i$, the equal-time canonical commutator is the distribution
$$[A_i(0,\mathbf x),E_j(0,\mathbf y)] =-i\,P_{T,ij}(-i\nabla_{\mathbf x})\delta^3(\mathbf x-\mathbf y).$$

lem-qft-photon-transverse-projector-kern.title: Newtonian off-diagonal kernel of the transverse projector

references.title: David Tong, Quantum Field Theory, Chapter 6, §6.2.1 Coulomb Gauge
references.locator: Complete author-hosted HTML chapter 6; equations 6.517–6.519 give the transverse projector commutator.

references.title: Mark Srednicki, Quantum Field Theory, author-hosted 2006 book draft, §55 Electrodynamics in Coulomb Gauge
references.locator: Complete 616-page book draft; equations 55.3–55.4 and 55.20 give the transverse projector and equal-time commutator. Conventions are translated explicitly here.

lem-qft-photon-transverse-projector-kern.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $G(\mathbf x)=1/(4\pi|\mathbf x|)$ on $\mathbb R^3\setminus\{0\}$, interpreted as its locally integrable distribution, and use the Fourier convention
$$\widehat f(\mathbf k)=\int_{\mathbb R^3}e^{-i\mathbf k\cdot\mathbf x}f(\mathbf x)\,d^3\mathbf x,\qquad f(\mathbf x)=(2\pi)^{-3}\int_{\mathbb R^3}e^{i\mathbf k\cdot\mathbf x}\widehat f(\mathbf k)\,d^3\mathbf k.$$
Then $\mathcal F^{-1}(|\mathbf k|^{-2})=G$ distributionally. Consequently, for $P_{T,ij}(\mathbf k)=\delta_{ij}-k_i k_j/|\mathbf k|^2$,
$$P_{T,ij}(-i\nabla)\delta^3 =\delta_{ij}\delta^3+\partial_i\partial_jG.$$
For $\mathbf x\ne0$,
$$\partial_i\partial_jG(\mathbf x) =-\frac{\delta_{ij}}{4\pi|\mathbf x|^3} +\frac{3x_ix_j}{4\pi|\mathbf x|^5}.$$
Thus the equal-time transverse-potential commutator of [[lem-qft-photon-smeared-potential]] has this off-diagonal Newtonian kernel (with its stated factor $-i$). The identity is distributional at the origin; the displayed classical derivative formula is only asserted away from it.

lem-qft-qed-conserved-current-gauge.title: Gauge-longitudinal kernel decoupling for explicit tree currents

references.title: David Tong, Quantum Field Theory, §6.4
references.locator: Complete author-hosted Chapter 6 HTML; explicit tree-level cancellation of longitudinal covariant-gauge propagator terms by on-shell Dirac currents.

references.title: Mark Srednicki, Quantum Field Theory, §§67–68
references.locator: Complete author-hosted draft; external-photon Ward identities and exact vertex relation, printed pp. 400–404. The present claim is only finite tree algebra.

lem-qft-qed-conserved-current-gauge.statement:
Let $p_1,p_1',p_2,p_2'$ be future-shell momenta for the same $\mu>0$ convention as [[lem-qft-qed-tree-ward]], and suppose $k=p_1-p_1'=p_2'-p_2$. Define
$$ J_1^\mu:=\bar u(p_1')\gamma^\mu u(p_1),\qquad J_2^\nu:=\bar u(p_2')\gamma^\nu u(p_2), $$
with the on-shell Dirac equations in [[lem-qft-qed-tree-ward]]. If a finite rational covariant-gauge kernel changes by $\Delta D_{\mu\nu}(k)=c(k)k_\mu k_\nu$, where $c(k)\in\mathbb C$ is finite at the chosen $k$, then
$$ J_1^\mu\Delta D_{\mu\nu}(k)J_2^\nu=0. $$
Likewise, for any conserved tree current $J^\mu$ of the forms proved in [[lem-qft-qed-tree-ward]], the contraction $\epsilon_\mu J^\mu$ is unchanged by $\epsilon^\mu\mapsto\epsilon^\mu+\alpha k^\mu$. These statements concern only the displayed finite tree-current contractions; they assert no gauge independence for arbitrary loop diagrams or renormalization schemes.

lem-qft-qed-coulomb-constraint.title: Gauss multiplier and smooth periodic Coulomb solver

references.title: David Tong, Quantum Field Theory, Chapter 6, §6.4
references.locator: Complete author-hosted HTML chapter 6; Coulomb gauge and the Gauss-law constraint.

references.title: Mark Srednicki, Quantum Field Theory, author-hosted 2006 book draft, §55
references.locator: Complete 616-page book draft; canonical Maxwell variables and Coulomb gauge.

lem-qft-qed-coulomb-constraint.statement:
Assume Countable Choice and the conventions of [[def-qft-qed-gauge-data]]. On the periodic box $T_L^3=(\mathbb R/L\mathbb Z)^3$, take smooth real periodic charge and current densities $\rho,\mathbf J$, smooth periodic $\mathbf A,\dot{\mathbf A},\phi$, and $L,\epsilon_0,\mu_0>0$. Define the formal classical density
$$\mathcal L=\frac{\epsilon_0}{2}|\dot{\mathbf A}+\nabla\phi|^2-\frac1{2\mu_0}|\nabla\times\mathbf A|^2-\rho\phi+\mathbf J\cdot\mathbf A.$$
The canonical momenta are $\boldsymbol\pi_A=\epsilon_0(\dot{\mathbf A}+\nabla\phi)$ and $\pi_\phi=0$. Periodic integration by parts gives
$$H=\int_{T_L^3}\left(\frac{|\boldsymbol\pi_A|^2}{2\epsilon_0}+\frac{|\nabla\times\mathbf A|^2}{2\mu_0} +\phi(\nabla\cdot\boldsymbol\pi_A+\rho)-\mathbf J\cdot\mathbf A\right)d^3x.$$
Variation of the multiplier $\phi$ imposes $\nabla\cdot\boldsymbol\pi_A+\rho=0$. In Coulomb gauge $\nabla\cdot\mathbf A=0$, this becomes $-\Delta\phi=\rho/\epsilon_0$. Such a smooth periodic solution exists only if $\int_{T_L^3}\rho\,d^3x=0$. If this neutrality condition holds, there is a unique zero-mean solution, with Fourier coefficients
$$\widehat\phi_0=0,\qquad \widehat\phi_k=\frac{\widehat\rho_k}{\epsilon_0|2\pi k/L|^2}\quad(k\ne0),\qquad \widehat\rho_k=L^{-3}\int_{[0,L]^3}\rho(x)e^{-2\pi i k\cdot x/L}\,d^3x.$$
It is smooth and satisfies
$$\frac{\epsilon_0}{2}\int|\nabla\phi|^2\,d^3x =\frac12\int\rho\phi\,d^3x =\frac{L^3}{2\epsilon_0}\sum_{k\ne0}\frac{|\widehat\rho_k|^2}{|2\pi k/L|^2}\ge0.$$
This is a classical conditional solver for smooth periodic neutral data; it makes no claim about quantum density products or nonperiodic boundary conditions.

lem-qft-qed-dirac-first-order-constraint.title: Finite-mode Dirac first-order constraint reduction

references.title: David Tong, Quantum Field Theory, Chapter 6, §6.1
references.locator: Complete author-hosted HTML chapter 6; first-order Dirac kinetic term and charged action.

references.title: Mark Srednicki, Quantum Field Theory, author-hosted 2006 book draft, §§36 and 57
references.locator: Complete 616-page book draft; Dirac kinetic term and QED coupling. This item states its distinct finite commuting-coordinate reduction explicitly.

lem-qft-qed-dirac-first-order-constraint.statement:
Assume Countable Choice, the constants in [[def-qft-qed-gauge-data]], $\hbar>0$, and a finite integer $N\ge1$. Let $z_j,\bar z_j$ be complex coordinate notation for the real and imaginary coordinates of $N$ commuting spinor-mode amplitudes. On the complexified canonical coordinate space impose
$$\{z_j,p_k\}=\delta_{jk},\qquad \{\bar z_j,\bar p_k\}=\delta_{jk},$$
with all other elementary brackets zero, extended by bilinearity and the Leibniz rule. The first-order kinetic term $\frac{i\hbar}{2}\sum_j(\bar z_j\dot z_j-\dot{\bar z}_jz_j)$ gives primary constraints
$$C_j=p_j-\frac{i\hbar}{2}\bar z_j,\qquad \bar C_j=\bar p_j+\frac{i\hbar}{2}z_j.$$
In the order $(C_1,\ldots,C_N,\bar C_1,\ldots,\bar C_N)$ their constraint matrix and inverse are
$$M=\begin{pmatrix}0&-i\hbar I_N\\i\hbar I_N&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad M^{-1}=\begin{pmatrix}0&-iI_N/\hbar\\iI_N/\hbar&0\end{pmatrix}.$$
Thus the constraints are second class. The Dirac bracket
$$\{F,G\}_D=\{F,G\}-\{F,\chi_A\}(M^{-1})_{AB}\{\chi_B,G\}, \quad \chi=(C_1,\ldots,C_N,\bar C_1,\ldots,\bar C_N),$$
satisfies $\{z_j,\bar z_k\}_D=-i\delta_{jk}/\hbar$ and $\{z_j,z_k\}_D=\{\bar z_j,\bar z_k\}_D=0$. For a real smooth finite-mode Hamiltonian $H(z,\bar z)$ the reduced equation is $i\hbar\dot z_j=\partial H/\partial\bar z_j$. These are ordinary commuting coordinates; they do not derive CAR by canonical quantization.

lem-qft-qed-dirac-gauge-current.title: Dirac gauge covariance, action and conserved current

references.title: David Tong, Quantum Field Theory, Chapter 6, §§6.1 and 6.3.1
references.locator: Complete author-hosted HTML chapter 6; QED gauge transformations, covariant derivative, Dirac action and current.

references.title: Mark Srednicki, Quantum Field Theory, author-hosted 2006 book draft, §§57–58
references.locator: Complete 616-page book draft; QED covariant derivative and charged Dirac coupling. Its metric and charge conventions are translated explicitly here.

lem-qft-qed-dirac-gauge-current.statement:
Assume Countable Choice and use the conventions of [[def-qft-qed-gauge-data]]. Let $a_a$ be a smooth real potential and let $\psi:\mathbb R^4\to\mathbb C^4$ be a smooth commuting spinor. Use the symmetrized classical density
$$\mathcal L_D=\frac i2\{\bar\psi\gamma^aD_a\psi-(D_a\bar\psi)\gamma^a\psi\}-\mu\bar\psi\psi,\qquad D_a\bar\psi=\partial_a\bar\psi+ig a_a\bar\psi.$$
For compactly supported smooth variations, its spinor Euler equation is $(i\gamma^aD_a-\mu)\psi=0$ and its adjoint. The density is invariant under the gauge transformation in [[def-qft-qed-gauge-data]]. On solutions,
$$\partial_a j^a=0,\qquad j^a=g\bar\psi\gamma^a\psi.$$
In SI variables the corresponding Hamiltonian density has the sign convention
$$\psi^\dagger\!\left[c\,\boldsymbol\alpha\cdot(-i\hbar\nabla-q\mathbf A)+\beta mc^2+q\phi\right]\psi.$$
These are conditional variational identities for smooth commuting classical fields. They assert no global existence theorem for the coupled field equations, no quantum current product, and no empirical measurement.

lem-qft-qed-formal-matrix-ward.title: Finite/formal gauge covariance and matrix Ward identity

references.title: David Tong, Quantum Field Theory, §§6.1.1 and 6.4
references.locator: Complete author-hosted Chapter 6 HTML; gauge transformation and finite QED propagator context.

references.title: Mark Srednicki, Quantum Field Theory, §§67–68
references.locator: Complete author-hosted draft; Ward identities in QED, printed pp. 400–404. The local item proves only finite/formal matrix identities.

lem-qft-qed-formal-matrix-ward.statement:
Let $K(z;\zeta)=K_0(\zeta)+zV(\zeta)$ and $S(z;\zeta)$ be the finite-dimensional formal matrices of [[def-qft-qed-formal-ring]], with $d\ge1$, $K_0(\zeta)$ invertible, and both coefficient matrices covariant under the vertex phase angles of [[def-qft-qed-finite-graph-gauge-data]]. Then $S$ is a two-sided inverse of $K$ in $M_d(\mathbb C\llbracket z\rrbracket)$, and
$$ S(z;\zeta^\theta)=D_\theta S(z;\zeta)D_\theta^{-1} $$
coefficientwise. For a differentiable phase path $D_s=e^{is\Theta}$, where the real vertex-angle path is $s\theta$, the variations satisfy
$$ \delta K=i[\Theta,K],\qquad \delta S=i[\Theta,S]=-S(\delta K)S . $$
For ordinary finite matrices $A,B\in GL_d(\mathbb C)$, the corresponding resolvent identity is $B^{-1}(B-A)A^{-1}=A^{-1}-B^{-1}$. These are formal or finite algebraic statements; they assert no convergence of a perturbation series, continuum limit, or loop Ward identity.

lem-qft-qed-grassmann-determinant.title: Finite Grassmann Gaussian and gauge-invariant determinant

references.title: Mark Srednicki, Quantum Field Theory, §44, Formal Development of Fermionic Path Integrals
references.locator: Complete author-hosted 616-page draft; finite Grassmann integration and complex Gaussian determinant, printed pp. 276–281.

references.title: David Tong, Quantum Field Theory, §§6.3.1 and 6.4
references.locator: Complete author-hosted Chapter 6 HTML; charged-fermion QED and finite-dimensional fermion propagator context.

lem-qft-qed-grassmann-determinant.statement:
Let $R=\mathbb C\llbracket z\rrbracket$, let $d\ge1$, and let $K\in M_d(R)$ be a finite matrix as in [[def-qft-qed-formal-ring]]. With $\mathcal I_d$ the top-coefficient functional of [[def-qft-qed-finite-grassmann-algebra]],
$$ \mathcal I_d\!\left(\exp\!\left(-\sum_{i,j=1}^d\bar\psi_iK_{ij}\psi_j\right)\right)=\det K. $$
If $D=\operatorname{diag}(u_1,\ldots,u_d)$ with each $u_i\in R^\times$ and $K'=DKD^{-1}$, then the finite Grassmann integral and determinant are gauge invariant: $\mathcal I_d(\exp(-\bar\psi K'\psi))=\det K'=\det K$. No infinite-dimensional Grassmann measure, continuum limit, or anomaly claim is made.

lem-qft-qed-tree-ward.title: Off-shell free Dirac Ward telescoping and tree currents

references.title: David Tong, Quantum Field Theory, §§6.3.1 and 6.4
references.locator: Complete author-hosted Chapter 6 HTML; charged Dirac current, free propagator symbols, and explicit tree-level current contractions.

references.title: Mark Srednicki, Quantum Field Theory, §§67–68
references.locator: Complete 616-page author-hosted draft; QED current Ward identities and exact propagator/vertex relation, printed pp. 400–404. The local result is restricted to rational finite matrices and on-shell tree currents.

lem-qft-qed-tree-ward.statement:
Use the $(-+++)$ coordinate convention, $h=-\eta=\operatorname{diag}(1,-1,-1,-1)$, and the Clifford matrices of [[def-qft-dirac-projections]]; the shell parameter $\mu>0$ has inverse-length units as in [[def-qft-scalar-mass-shell]]. For $p=(p^0,\mathbf p)\in\mathbb R^4$, write
$$ \Gamma(p):=\gamma^0p^0-\sum_{j=1}^3\gamma^jp_j,\qquad K(p):=\Gamma(p)-\mu I_4. $$
When $h(p,p)\ne\mu^2$, define the finite rational inverse
$$ S_0(p):=\frac{\Gamma(p)+\mu I_4}{h(p,p)-\mu^2}. $$
For $p,p+k$ with both denominators nonzero,
$$ S_0(p+k)\Gamma(k)S_0(p)=S_0(p)-S_0(p+k). $$
For any finite chain of off-shell momenta, the corresponding insertion differences telescope with both endpoint terms retained. If $u(p),u(p')$ satisfy $(\Gamma(p)-\mu)u(p)=0$, $(\Gamma(p')-\mu)u(p')=0$ and $p,p'$ lie on the future shell, then $\bar u(p')\Gamma(p-p')u(p)=0$, where $\bar u=u^\dagger\beta$. If $v(q)$ satisfies $(\Gamma(q)+\mu)v(q)=0$ on the future shell, then $\bar v(q)\Gamma(p+q)u(p)=0$. These are finite rational/tree identities; no Feynman boundary value, singular distribution product, loop theorem, or all-diagram gauge-independence claim is included.

lem-qft-scalar-causal-commutator.title: Causal support of the scalar commutator distribution

references.title: David Tong, Quantum Field Theory, section 2.6.1
references.locator: Author-hosted HTML text of chapter 2, section 2.6.1, equations 2.160–2.167; the complete lecture-note set is also listed as a 155-page PDF.

references.title: Fewster and Rejzner, Algebraic Quantum Field Theory—an introduction
references.locator: Complete 47-page article, version 2; section 4.2, PDF pages 14–18, causal propagator and free scalar Weyl algebra.

lem-qft-scalar-causal-commutator.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. For $\mu\ge0$, define the tempered distribution
$$\Delta_\mu(t,\mathbf x)= \int_{\mathbb R^3}\frac{d^3\mathbf k}{(2\pi)^3} \frac{\sin(\omega_\mu(\mathbf k)t)}{\omega_\mu(\mathbf k)} e^{i\mathbf k\cdot\mathbf x},$$
with the massless integrand defined off $\mathbf k=0$; its $1/|\mathbf k|$
behavior is locally integrable in three dimensions. Then
$$\operatorname{supp}\Delta_\mu \subseteq\{(t,\mathbf x):t^2-|\mathbf x|^2\ge0\},$$
the closed causal cone for the $(-+++)$ metric. For real compactly supported
smooth $f,g$, put
$$\Delta_\mu(f,g)= \int_{\mathbb R^4}\!\int_{\mathbb R^4} f(x)g(y)\Delta_\mu(x-y)\,d^4x\,d^4y.$$
On $\mathcal D_{\rm fin}$ the smeared fields of
[[lem-qft-smeared-free-scalar]] satisfy
$$[\Phi_\mu(f),\Phi_\mu(g)]=-i\Delta_\mu(f,g)I.$$
Consequently spacelike-separated supports give commuting fields.

lem-qft-scalar-local-weyl-algebra.title: Isotony and spacelike commutativity of scalar local Weyl algebras

references.title: Fewster and Rejzner, Algebraic Quantum Field Theory—an introduction
references.locator: Complete 47-page article, version 2; section 4.2 and PDF pages 14–18, free scalar Weyl algebra and local nets.

references.title: David Tong, Quantum Field Theory, section 2.6.1
references.locator: Author-hosted HTML text of chapter 2, section 2.6.1, equations 2.160–2.167; the complete lecture-note set is also listed as a 155-page PDF.

lem-qft-scalar-local-weyl-algebra.statement:
Assume Countable Choice [[def-countable-choice]].
Let $O\subseteq\mathbb R^4$ be open. For real
$f\in C_c^\infty(O)$ define
$$W_\mu(f):=W_{\rm Segal}(\sqrt2K_\mu f),$$
where the Segal normalization is exactly
$\Phi_{\rm Segal}(h)=(a^\dagger(h)+a(h))/\sqrt2$ on the finite-particle
domain, as in [[lem-qft-segal-weyl-domain]]. This scale makes the generator
of $t\mapsto W_\mu(tf)$ equal to the real scalar field
$\Phi_\mu(f)=a(K_\mu f)+a^\dagger(K_\mu f)$ of
[[lem-qft-smeared-free-scalar]]. Define the unital norm-closed operator
algebra
$$\mathfrak A_\mu(O)= \overline{\operatorname{alg}}^{\|\cdot\|} \{I,W_\mu(f),W_\mu(f)^*:f\in C_c^\infty(O;\mathbb R)\}.$$
Then $O_1\subseteq O_2$ implies
$\mathfrak A_\mu(O_1)\subseteq\mathfrak A_\mu(O_2)$. If every difference
$x-y$, with $x\in O_1$ and $y\in O_2$, is spacelike, then every element of
$\mathfrak A_\mu(O_1)$ commutes with every element of
$\mathfrak A_\mu(O_2)$. These are algebraic properties of the constructed
representation; they are not empirical signaling or measurement claims.

lem-qft-scalar-poincare-action.title: Strongly continuous scalar one-particle Poincare action

references.title: David Tong, Quantum Field Theory, author-hosted HTML text of chapter 2
references.locator: Sections 2.4.1 and 2.6, relativistic one-particle normalization and the Poincare-covariant Heisenberg field.

references.title: Mark Srednicki, Quantum Field Theory, author draft, chapters 3–4
references.locator: Complete 616-page author-hosted draft; chapter 3 relativistic shell normalization and chapter 4 free scalar modes.

lem-qft-scalar-poincare-action.statement:
Assume Countable Choice [[def-countable-choice]]. Use the proper
orthochronous Poincare group
$G=\mathbb R^4\rtimes SO^+(1,3)$ in the coordinates of
[[def-qft-scalar-mass-shell]]. For $g=(a,\Lambda)\in G$, define
$$f_g(x)=f(\Lambda^{-1}(x-a)),\qquad [U_\mu(g)h](p)=e^{ip\circ a}h(\Lambda^{-1}p).$$
Then $f_g\in\mathscr S(\mathbb R^4)$, $U_\mu(g)$ is a well-defined unitary
on $H_\mu$, $g\mapsto U_\mu(g)$ is a strongly continuous representation, and
$$K_\mu f_g=U_\mu(g)K_\mu f \qquad(f\in\mathscr S(\mathbb R^4)).$$
The group product convention is
$(a,\Lambda)(b,\Gamma)=(a+\Lambda b,\Lambda\Gamma)$.

post-qft-example-formal-observable-map.title: Formal diagram coefficient-to-observable adoption
post-qft-example-formal-observable-map.physical_scope: A model-specific phenomenological reading of named formal tree coefficients through the stated two-body flux and phase-space maps. It adopts no exact continuum scattering operator, LSZ limit, convergence estimate, loop or soft-radiation correction, detector model, or empirical result.

references.title: David Tong, Quantum Field Theory, Chapter 3 §§3.5.3 and 3.6.2–3.6.3, and Chapter 6 §6.6
David Tong, Quantum Field Theory, Chapter 6 §§6.4.1, 6.5 and 6.6
Mark Srednicki, Quantum Field Theory, author-hosted prepublication draft, §§11, 46–48, 59 and 64
X. Fan et al., Measurement of the Electron Magnetic Moment, Physical Review Letters 130, 071801 (2023), arXiv:2209.13084v2

post-qft-example-formal-observable-map.statement:
For a specifically named finite tree calculation, adopt its selected formal
diagram coefficient as a **leading perturbative coefficient** with a stated
phenomenological reading. For QED, use the vertex and free-line conventions
of the current draft supplier
[[post-qft-formal-qed-coefficients]]. A particle of natural charge $q_n$ has
vertex $iq_n\gamma^a$; the electron has $q_n=-e_n$ and vertex
$-ie_n\gamma^a$. The rational fermion line is
$$ i\frac{\not p+\mu}{h(p,p)-\mu^2}, $$
for $\mu>0$ and off-shell $p$ with $h(p,p)-\mu^2\ne0$. In Feynman gauge
the auxiliary photon line is
$$ -i\frac{h_{ab}}{h(k,k)+i0}=i\frac{\eta_{ab}}{h(k,k)+i0}. $$
For a finite matrix kernel the coefficientwise inverse in
[[post-qft-formal-qed-coefficients]] is part of the formal convention and
asserts no convergence. If a time-ordered distribution is used, use the
actual free carrier specified there; that identification is conditional on
[[def-countable-choice]]. The displayed pole notation does not define loop
products. In the pair-production channel below the selected muon also has
model charge $-e$, and only the photon line is internal.

For declared incoming spin probabilities, sum over declared final spin
labels, and a specified formal amplitude $\mathcal A$, adopt the
cross-section coefficient map of
[[lem-qft-example-two-body-phase-space]]. In the center-of-momentum frame it
uses the invariant incoming flux $F$, the two-body measure $d\Phi_2$, and the
final-state factor $S_f=2$ for identical particles or $S_f=1$ for
distinguishable particles, integrated over the full labeled sphere. When
this coefficient is read phenomenologically, the initial preparation,
channel, threshold, and approximation are part of the model statement. No
universal error estimate for omitted terms is implied.

For the scalar examples, separately adopt the constant formal amplitudes
$\mathcal A=-\lambda$ for the quartic contact channel and $\mathcal G=G_E$
for the cubic parent decay, with the units and external normalization stated
at each use. Their coefficient map is the one in
[[lem-qft-example-two-body-phase-space]]. If a rate $\Gamma$ is reported as
an energy width, the convention is explicitly $\Gamma_E:=\hbar\Gamma$; it
does not supply a survival law.

The readings above do not identify a formal coefficient with an exact
continuum cross section, probability, decay rate, or measured estimate. In
particular they do not construct an interacting continuum $S$-matrix or LSZ
limit, establish convergence of a perturbation series, bound loop or
soft-radiation effects, specify beam or detector cuts, resolve threshold
resummation, or reproduce the statistical analysis of an experiment. A
comparison with observations would require the actual apparatus, sampling,
calibration, uncertainty, and radiative-inclusiveness conditions. The
reported electron magnetic-moment measurements, including the Fan et al.
report listed in the source references, remain source-reported
empirical results and are not premises of this adoption.

post-qft-free-photon-model.title: Positive transverse free photon model
post-qft-free-photon-model.physical_scope: The selected source-free, flat Minkowski Maxwell photon model with a positive transverse one-particle Hilbert space, its constructed bosonic Fock representation and free dynamics, and actual smeared field-strength and bounded Weyl observables; no interacting continuum QED or empirical outcome is asserted.

references.title: David Tong, Quantum Field Theory, author-hosted full-text Chapter 6
references.locator: §6.1 for the source-free Maxwell field; §6.2, especially §6.2.1, for Coulomb-gauge transverse modes, the two physical polarizations, and the auxiliary Lorenz-gauge construction.

references.title: Mark Srednicki, Quantum Field Theory, author-hosted 2006 prepublication book draft
references.locator: §§54–55, printed pp. 332–338, for the Maxwell potential, Coulomb-gauge transverse projector, free modes, two helicities, and Hamiltonian. The source uses Heaviside–Lorentz units and c=1; the adopted model retains the explicit SI conversion.

post-qft-free-photon-model.statement:
Adopt the following specified free-photon model in the oriented,
time-oriented affine Minkowski spacetime and length coordinates of
[[def-qft-framework-units]], with metric $(-,+,+,+)$ and $x^0=ct$. The
classical electromagnetic input is the smooth source-free branch of
[[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]]; the electromagnetic two-form and its potential
components are those of [[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]], and a supplied
potential is subject to [[def-em-gauge-transformation]]. These EM suppliers
are physical input and conventions: they do not by themselves construct a
quantum representation.

For almost every $\mathbf k\in\mathbb R^3\setminus\{0\}$, set
$\mathbf n=\mathbf k/|\mathbf k|$ and
$P_T(\mathbf k)=I_3-\mathbf n\mathbf n^{\mathsf T}$. The mathematical

Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]) for the finite-regulator
spectral and trace construction. For the fixed model of
[[post-qft-regulated-polynomial-model]] and a declared
temperature input $T>0$, use
[[def-qft-regulated-thermal-parameter]] to set
$\beta_{\rm phys}=(k_BT)^{-1}$ and
$\widehat\beta=E_*\beta_{\rm phys}>0$. Let $h$ be the model's specified
self-adjoint form realization and $H_{\rm phys}=E_*h$. When the finite-mode
coercivity hypotheses hold, [[thm-qft-regulated-gibbs-trace]] proves that
$e^{-\widehat\beta h}$ is positive trace class with finite positive trace.
Adopt the normalized operator

$$\rho_T:=\frac{e^{-\beta_{\rm phys}H_{\rm phys}}}{Z_T},\qquad Z_T:=\operatorname{Tr}(e^{-\beta_{\rm phys}H_{\rm phys}})$$

as this finite-regulator model's canonical equilibrium state. This is a
physical state assignment, not a deduction that the dynamics reach
equilibrium. It asserts no infinite-volume trace, no zero-temperature state,
and no empirical observation.

citations.quote:
The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

Assume Countable Choice [[def-countable-choice]]. Here
$\mathscr S(\mathbb R^4)$ is the Schwartz space of smooth complex functions
whose coordinate-weighted derivatives are all bounded, as defined in
[[def-schwartz-space-and-its-seminorms]].
Fix an oriented, time-oriented affine Minkowski space and an inertial coordinate
chart as in [[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]] and
[[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]]. Use coordinates
$x=(x^0,\mathbf x)$ and metric $\eta=\mathrm{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, matching the
$(-+++)$ convention of the SR suppliers. Some QFT sources use its negative
$(+---)$; the Lorentz group is unchanged, and the phase is fixed explicitly
below.
Coordinates $x$ have length units, momenta have inverse-length units, and the
Fourier phase below is dimensionless. A parameter $\mu\ge0$ has inverse-length
units and is only a mathematical shell parameter; it is not identified with a
physical rest mass. For $\mathbf k\in\mathbb R^3$, set
$$\omega_\mu(\mathbf k)=\sqrt{|\mathbf k|^2+\mu^2},\qquad p_\mu(\mathbf k)=(\omega_\mu(\mathbf k),\mathbf k).$$
The future mass shell is
$$H_\mu^+=\{(p^0,\mathbf p): (p^0)^2-|\mathbf p|^2=\mu^2,\ p^0>0\}.$$
When $\mu=0$, its apex is omitted; thus $\mathbf k\ne0$ in the massless
parameterization. The scalar shell pairing is
$$p\circ x:=p^0x^0-\mathbf p\cdot\mathbf x=-\eta(p,x).$$
Define the measure and one-particle Hilbert space by
$$d\nu_\mu(p_\mu(\mathbf k))= \frac{d^3\mathbf k}{(2\pi)^3\,2\omega_\mu(\mathbf k)},\qquad H_\mu=L^2(H_\mu^+,d\nu_\mu;\mathbb C),$$
where the omitted massless apex has measure zero. For $f\in\mathscr S(\mathbb
R^4)$ define its pointwise shell Fourier restriction by
$$K_\mu f(p)=\int_{\mathbb R^4}f(x)e^{ip\circ x}\,d^4x.$$
The Fourier convention is exactly the displayed integral, with no prefactor.
If $\widehat f(\xi^0,\boldsymbol\xi)=
\int f(x)e^{-2\pi i(x^0\xi^0+\mathbf x\cdot\boldsymbol\xi)}\,d^4x$ denotes
the standard transform in
[[cor-fourier-transform-is-a-topological-automorphism-of-schwartz-space]],
then
$$\mathcal F_+f(p^0,\mathbf p):=\int f(x)e^{i(p^0x^0-\mathbf p\cdot\mathbf x)}\,d^4x =\widehat f\!\left(-\frac{p^0}{2\pi},\frac{\mathbf p}{2\pi}\right).$$
Its inverse is
$$f(x)=(2\pi)^{-4}\int_{\mathbb R^4} \mathcal F_+f(p^0,\mathbf p)e^{-i(p^0x^0-\mathbf p\cdot\mathbf x)} \,dp^0\,d^3\mathbf p.$$
Thus this convention is a time reflection and rescaling of the cited
Schwartz automorphism and has the stated reciprocal normalization.
The proper orthochronous Lorentz group consists of linear maps preserving
$\eta$, orientation and the chosen future cone. A Poincare map is
$x\mapsto a+\Lambda x$ with $a\in\mathbb R^4$ and $\Lambda$ in that group.

This is a mathematical free scalar one-particle construction. It adopts the
chosen coordinates, measure and Fourier convention; it asserts no experimental
observation, physical mass identification or measurement outcome.

An **oriented time-oriented affine Minkowski space** is a quadruple
$(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ with the following data. In this notation $V$ includes its
specified orientation; forgetting that orientation gives only the underlying
real vector space, not the full datum $V$ of the model.

1. A nonempty affine space $A$ over a $4$-dimensional real vector space $V$,
   with action $(p,v)\mapsto p+v$ and displacement $q-p\in V$
   ([[def-affine-space-and-displacement]]). In particular $V$ is a real vector
   space of dimension $4$.
2. A Lorentz form $\eta$ on $V$, i.e. a nondegenerate symmetric bilinear form of
   inertia $(3,1,0)$ ([[def-lorentz-form-and-inertia]]). Its associated quadratic
   form is $q(v)=\eta(v,v)$.
3. An **orientation** of $V$: a positive ray of the determinant line
   $\Lambda^4V$, fixed once and for all
   ([[def-determinant-line-orientation-of-a-finite-dimensional-real-vector-space]]).
4. A **time orientation** $C^+$ of $(V,\eta)$: one of the two connected
   components of the timelike set $T=\{v\in V:\eta(v,v)<0\}$, the other being
   $C^-:=T\setminus C^+$ ([[def-time-orientation-and-future-causal-sets]]).

The following terminology is attached to such a quadruple.

- The elements $p$ of $A$ are the **events**; for events $p,q$ the vector
  $q-p\in V$ is the **displacement from $p$ to $q$**.
- The **interval** of $p,q\in A$ is the real number
  $I(p,q):=\eta(q-p,q-p)=q(q-p)$.
- Events $p,q$ are **timelike**, **null**, **spacelike** or **causally
  related** when the displacement $q-p$ is timelike, null, spacelike or causal
  in the sense of [[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]]; they are
  **future-related** when $q-p$ is future causal and **past-related** when
  $q-p$ is past causal in the sense of
  [[def-time-orientation-and-future-causal-sets]].

**No point of $A$ is distinguished.** For every $v\in V$ the translation
$\tau_v:A\to A$, $\tau_v(p):=p+v$, is a bijection, since it is inverse to
$\tau_{-v}$: $\tau_{-v}(\tau_v(p))=(p+v)+(-v)=p+(v-v)=p$ and symmetrically, by
the affine action axioms ([[def-affine-space-and-displacement]]). Displacements
are translation invariant, $\tau_v(q)-\tau_v(p)=q-p$, so every $\tau_v$ preserves
the interval, the causal classification of every ordered pair, and the sets
$C^+$, $C^-$ (which are subsets of $V$, independent of the point of $A$); it
changes only the labelling of points. The mathematical structure of the model is
exactly the quadruple $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$; no derived physical quantity (proper
time, four-velocity, momentum, energy, charge or any field) is part of this
definition, and all later structure of the framework (frames, charts, tensor
fields, worldlines) is built on this model.

**Well-definedness.** The affine-space definition supplies the action and the
unique displacements; the Lorentz-form definition supplies $\eta$ and its
inertia; the determinant-line definition supplies orientations; and the two
components of $T$ between which the time-orientation definition chooses exist by
the components lemma recorded in the well-definedness clause of
[[def-time-orientation-and-future-causal-sets]], which is also what makes the
names future and past causal in item 4 well defined.

Let $V$ be a $4$-dimensional real vector space ([[def-vector-space]],
[[def-dimension]]). A **Lorentz form** on $V$ is a symmetric bilinear form
$\eta:V\times V\to\mathbb R$ ([[def-bilinear-symmetric-skew-and-alternating-forms]])
such that

1. $\eta$ is nondegenerate: both radicals
   $\operatorname{rad}_L(\eta)=\{u:\eta(u,v)=0\text{ for every }v\}$ and
   $\operatorname{rad}_R(\eta)=\{v:\eta(u,v)=0\text{ for every }u\}$ are
   $\{0\}$ ([[def-matrix-radicals-rank-and-nondegeneracy-of-a-bilinear-form]]);
   and
2. $\eta$ has **inertia** $(3,1,0)$: in some (equivalently, in every) basis of
   $V$ in which the matrix of $\eta$ is diagonal, exactly three diagonal
   entries are positive, exactly one is negative, and none is zero
   ([[def-definiteness-inertia-and-signature-data-over-the-reals]]).

The inertia of a symmetric bilinear form is the triple $(p,q,r)$ of numbers of
positive, negative and zero diagonal entries of any diagonalizing basis, and it
is independent of the diagonalizing basis by Sylvester's law of inertia
([[def-definiteness-inertia-and-signature-data-over-the-reals]]); hence clause 2
is a property of $\eta$ itself and not of a chosen basis. The **associated
quadratic form** of $\eta$ is

$$q(v):=\eta(v,v),\qquad v\in V .$$

A **Lorentz vector space of signature $(-,+,+,+)$** is a pair $(V,\eta)$
consisting of a $4$-dimensional real vector space $V$ and a Lorentz form $\eta$
on $V$; the name records that the diagonal normal form of $\eta$ has one
negative entry followed by three positive entries. No positive-definite
structure on $V$ is assumed or implied by this definition, and $q$ takes both
negative and positive values on nonzero vectors: a basis in which
$\eta$ is diagonal with diagonal entries $-1,1,1,1$ exists by clause 2, and on
its first vector $q$ is $-1$, while on each of the other three it is $+1$.

Let $(V,\eta)$ be a Lorentz vector space of signature $(-,+,+,+)$
([[def-lorentz-form-and-inertia]]), with causal terminology as in
[[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]], and let

$$T:=\{v\in V:\eta(v,v)<0\}$$

be its **timelike set**. Components and closures refer to the topology obtained
by using any ordered basis to identify $V$ with Euclidean $\mathbb R^4$;
[[lem-timelike-cone-has-two-convex-components]], step 5.1, proves that the
resulting open sets are independent of the basis. By that lemma the
set $T$ has exactly two connected components, and each of them is nonempty,
open, convex and path-connected. A **time orientation** of $(V,\eta)$ is a
choice of one of these two components. Fixing such a choice, write $C^+$ for the
chosen component and

$$C^-:=T\setminus C^+$$

for the other component; thus $T=C^+\sqcup C^-$ is a disjoint union and
$C^+$, $C^-$ are exactly the two components supplied by the lemma. Relative to
this choice a vector $v\in V$ is

- **future timelike** when $v\in C^+$;
- **past timelike** when $v\in C^-$;
- **future null** when $v\neq 0$, $\eta(v,v)=0$ and $v\in\operatorname{cl}(C^+)$;
- **past null** when $v\neq 0$, $\eta(v,v)=0$ and $v\in\operatorname{cl}(C^-)$;
- **future causal** when it is future timelike or future null;
- **past causal** when it is past timelike or past null.

The sets $\operatorname{cl}(C^+)$ and $\operatorname{cl}(C^-)$ are the
**future closed cone** and the **past closed cone** of the time-oriented space
$(V,\eta,C^+)$. By [[lem-timelike-cone-has-two-convex-components]] each of them
is a convex cone, their intersection is $\{0\}$, and a vector is causal exactly
when it is future causal or past causal, in which case exactly one of these two
alternatives holds: no nonzero vector is both future causal and past causal.
The timelike vectors are exactly the points of $T=C^+\cup C^-$, and
$0\notin T$ because $\eta(0,0)=0$; since a null vector is nonzero with
$\eta(v,v)=0$, no vector is both timelike and null, so the classes above are
mutually exclusive where the definitions say they are: no vector is both future
and past causal, and no timelike vector is null.

Let $(V,\eta)$ be a Lorentz vector space of signature $(-,+,+,+)$
([[def-lorentz-form-and-inertia]]), with associated quadratic form
$q(v)=\eta(v,v)$. A vector $v\in V$ is

- **timelike** when $q(v)<0$;
- **null**, or **lightlike**, when $v\neq 0$ and $q(v)=0$;
- **spacelike** when $q(v)>0$;
- **causal** when it is timelike or null.

The zero vector $0\in V$ satisfies $q(0)=0$ and is consequently **none** of
timelike, null or spacelike: the null case explicitly excludes it, and the
timelike and spacelike cases exclude it by $q(0)=0$ together with the strict
inequalities. The **causal character** of a nonzero vector $v$ is the sign of
the real number $q(v)$, and the three names are attached to the three signs as
above. When no confusion arises, the pairing $\eta$ itself is written
$\langle v,w\rangle:=\eta(v,w)$.

**Each nonzero vector has exactly one causal character.** For a nonzero
$v\in V$ the real number $q(v)$ satisfies exactly one of $q(v)<0$, $q(v)=0$,
$q(v)>0$ by trichotomy of the order on $\mathbb R$, so $v$ is timelike, null or
spacelike, and no two of the three alternatives can hold at once. The causal
vectors are therefore exactly the nonzero vectors that are timelike or null,
and the zero vector is causal in no sense introduced here.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let
$U,V \subseteq \mathbb R^n$ be open and let $T : U \to V$ be a
$C^1$ diffeomorphism. For every nonnegative Lebesgue measurable
$f : V \to [0,\infty]$,
$$ \int_V f(y)\,d\lambda_n(y) = \int_U f(T(x))\,|\det DT(x)|\,d\lambda_n(x). $$

derivations.claim:
On $\mathbf k\ne0$ if $\mu=0$, and on all $\mathbf k$ if $\mu>0$,
$F_\mu$ is a smooth chart of the shell. On every compact subset of this chart
the density $[(2\pi)^3 2\omega_\mu]^{-1}$ is bounded; for $\mu=0$ near the
omitted apex it is proportional to $|\mathbf k|^{-1}$, whose integral over a
radius-$r$ ball is proportional to $\int_0^r s\,ds<\infty$. Compact annuli,
and for $\mu>0$ compact balls, give a countable cover by finite-measure sets;
hence $d\nu_\mu$ is locally finite and sigma-finite.

Fix $\Lambda$ and write $F=F_\mu$, $F(\mathbf k')=\Lambda F(\mathbf k)$.
Because $\Lambda$ preserves the future shell, this defines a smooth
diffeomorphism $\mathbf k\mapsto\mathbf k'$ on the chart; let
$J=D\mathbf k'/D\mathbf k$. Put $q_0=(1,0,0,0)$. The columns of
$[q_0,DF(\mathbf k)]$ have determinant $1$. Differentiating
$\Lambda F(\mathbf k)=F(\mathbf k')$ gives
$\Lambda DF(\mathbf k)=DF(\mathbf k')J$, and therefore
$$1=\det[\Lambda q_0,DF(\mathbf k')]\det J.$$
For any $u\in\mathbb R^4$, direct expansion of the determinant gives
$\det[u,DF(\mathbf k')]=-\eta(u,F(\mathbf k'))/\omega_\mu(\mathbf k')$.
Take $u=\Lambda q_0$. Metric preservation and
$F(\mathbf k')=\Lambda F(\mathbf k)$ imply
$-\eta(\Lambda q_0,F(\mathbf k'))=-\eta(q_0,F(\mathbf k))
=\omega_\mu(\mathbf k)$. Thus $\det J=\omega_\mu(\mathbf k')/
\omega_\mu(\mathbf k)>0$.

The change-of-variables theorem [F3] and the Jacobian from 2.1 give
$$\frac{d^3\mathbf k'}{\omega_\mu(\mathbf k')} =\frac{\det J\,d^3\mathbf k}{\omega_\mu(\mathbf k')} =\frac{d^3\mathbf k}{\omega_\mu(\mathbf k)}.$$
Multiplication by the constant $[2(2\pi)^3]^{-1}$ proves invariance for
nonnegative Borel functions. The massless apex is a
single omitted point and was never in the chart; the locally finite density
has no extra point mass there.

derivations.claim:
In the chart $\mathbf k\mapsto p_\mu(\mathbf k)$, write
$w_\mu(\mathbf k)=[2(2\pi)^3\omega_\mu(\mathbf k)]^{-1}$. Multiplication by
$\sqrt{w_\mu}$ is an isometry from $H_\mu$ onto
$L^2(\mathbb R^3\setminus\{0\},d^3\mathbf k)$ (for $\mu=0$) or
$L^2(\mathbb R^3,d^3\mathbf k)$ (for $\mu>0$), with inverse division by

R^3)$ is separable by [F1]. In the massless case extend any function on the
punctured space by zero at the null point, approximate it by the countable
dense family from [F1], and restrict those approximants back to the punctured
space; restriction does not increase the norm. Thus both chart spaces, and
therefore $H_\mu$, are separable.

$\Omega=\mathbb R^3\setminus\{0\}$ for $\mu=0$. For
$\Omega_n=\{1/n<|\mathbf k|<n\}$, these sets increase to $\Omega\setminus\{0\}$; its complement in $\Omega$ is null for the shell measure.

shows $\|h\mathbf1_{\Omega\setminus\Omega_n}\|_{L^2(w_\mu)}\to0$.

statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

Assume Countable Choice [[def-countable-choice]]. Here
$\mathscr S(\mathbb R^4)$ is the Schwartz space of smooth complex functions
whose coordinate-weighted derivatives are all bounded, as defined in
[[def-schwartz-space-and-its-seminorms]].
Fix an oriented, time-oriented affine Minkowski space and an inertial coordinate
chart as in [[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]] and
[[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]]. Use coordinates
$x=(x^0,\mathbf x)$ and metric $\eta=\mathrm{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, matching the
$(-+++)$ convention of the SR suppliers. Some QFT sources use its negative
$(+---)$; the Lorentz group is unchanged, and the phase is fixed explicitly
below.
Coordinates $x$ have length units, momenta have inverse-length units, and the
Fourier phase below is dimensionless. A parameter $\mu\ge0$ has inverse-length
units and is only a mathematical shell parameter; it is not identified with a
physical rest mass. For $\mathbf k\in\mathbb R^3$, set
$$\omega_\mu(\mathbf k)=\sqrt{|\mathbf k|^2+\mu^2},\qquad p_\mu(\mathbf k)=(\omega_\mu(\mathbf k),\mathbf k).$$
The future mass shell is
$$H_\mu^+=\{(p^0,\mathbf p): (p^0)^2-|\mathbf p|^2=\mu^2,\ p^0>0\}.$$
When $\mu=0$, its apex is omitted; thus $\mathbf k\ne0$ in the massless
parameterization. The scalar shell pairing is
$$p\circ x:=p^0x^0-\mathbf p\cdot\mathbf x=-\eta(p,x).$$
Define the measure and one-particle Hilbert space by
$$d\nu_\mu(p_\mu(\mathbf k))= \frac{d^3\mathbf k}{(2\pi)^3\,2\omega_\mu(\mathbf k)},\qquad H_\mu=L^2(H_\mu^+,d\nu_\mu;\mathbb C),$$
where the omitted massless apex has measure zero. For $f\in\mathscr S(\mathbb
R^4)$ define its pointwise shell Fourier restriction by
$$K_\mu f(p)=\int_{\mathbb R^4}f(x)e^{ip\circ x}\,d^4x.$$
The Fourier convention is exactly the displayed integral, with no prefactor.
If $\widehat f(\xi^0,\boldsymbol\xi)=
\int f(x)e^{-2\pi i(x^0\xi^0+\mathbf x\cdot\boldsymbol\xi)}\,d^4x$ denotes
the standard transform in
[[cor-fourier-transform-is-a-topological-automorphism-of-schwartz-space]],
then
$$\mathcal F_+f(p^0,\mathbf p):=\int f(x)e^{i(p^0x^0-\mathbf p\cdot\mathbf x)}\,d^4x =\widehat f\!\left(-\frac{p^0}{2\pi},\frac{\mathbf p}{2\pi}\right).$$
Its inverse is
$$f(x)=(2\pi)^{-4}\int_{\mathbb R^4} \mathcal F_+f(p^0,\mathbf p)e^{-i(p^0x^0-\mathbf p\cdot\mathbf x)} \,dp^0\,d^3\mathbf p.$$

Schwartz automorphism and has the stated reciprocal normalization.

$\eta$, orientation and the chosen future cone. A Poincare map is
$x\mapsto a+\Lambda x$ with $a\in\mathbb R^4$ and $\Lambda$ in that group.

This is a mathematical free scalar one-particle construction. It adopts the
chosen coordinates, measure and Fourier convention; it asserts no experimental
observation, physical mass identification or measurement outcome.

Fix an integer $n\ge1$. With the complex smooth-function convention of [[def-complex-lp-and-euclidean-test-function-conventions]] and multi-indices of [[def-ck-and-multi-index-notation-in-several-variables]], define
$$p_{\alpha\beta}(f)=\sup_{x\in\mathbb R^n}|x^\alpha\partial^\beta f(x)|,\qquad \mathcal S(\mathbb R^n)=\{f\in C^\infty(\mathbb R^n;\mathbb C):p_{\alpha\beta}(f)<\infty\text{ for all }\alpha,\beta\}.$$
The zero multi-index gives $x^0=1$ and $\partial^0f=f$. These are actual smooth functions, not equivalence classes. The notation $C_c^\infty$ uses the support convention in [[def-c-c-and-c-c-infinity-on-rn]].

Pointwise differentiation is linear; thus $p_{\alpha\beta}(f+g)\le p_{\alpha\beta}(f)+p_{\alpha\beta}(g)$ and $p_{\alpha\beta}(cf)=|c|p_{\alpha\beta}(f)$. In particular this set is a complex vector space and each $p_{\alpha\beta}$ is a seminorm. The zero function belongs to it. Since $p_{00}(f)=0$ forces $f(x)=0$ for every $x$, the family separates functions. No choice principle is needed.
Assume countable choice. The Fourier transform is a topological automorphism of $\mathcal S(\mathbb R^n)$, with $\mathcal F^2=R$ and $\mathcal F^{-1}=R\mathcal F$, where $Rf(x)=f(-x)$.

Assume countable choice. The negative-sign, $2\pi$-normalized Fourier transform is continuous $\mathcal F:\mathcal S\to\mathcal S$, and
$$\mathcal F(\partial^\alpha f)(\xi)=(2\pi i\xi)^\alpha\widehat f(\xi),\qquad \partial^\beta\widehat f=\mathcal F((-2\pi ix)^\beta f).$$

derivations.claim:
Define the continuous Schwartz seminorm
$$q_2(f)=\sup_{p\in\mathbb R^4}(1+|p|)^2|\mathcal F_+f(p)|.$$
Continuity follows from [F3,F4] and [F2]. On shell,
$|\mathcal F_+f(p_\mu(\mathbf k))|
\le q_2(f)(1+|\mathbf k|)^{-2}$ because
$|p_\mu(\mathbf k)|\ge|\mathbf k|$. Hence
$$\|K_\mu f\|_{H_\mu}^2 \le\frac{q_2(f)^2}{2(2\pi)^3} \int_{\mathbb R^3} \frac{(1+|\mathbf k|)^{-4}}{\omega_\mu(\mathbf k)}\,d^3\mathbf k.$$
The integral is finite: in polar coordinates its radial integrand is
$r^2(1+r)^{-4}/\sqrt{r^2+\mu^2}$, which is $O(r)$ near $0$ when $\mu=0$,
is $O(r^2)$ near $0$ when $\mu>0$, and is $O(r^{-3})$ at infinity.
Therefore $K_\mu f\in H_\mu$, and the displayed seminorm bound proves
continuity and linearity.

By [F4], applying $\partial_0^2-\Delta+\mu^2$ before $\mathcal F_+$
multiplies by $-(p^0)^2+|\mathbf p|^2+\mu^2$. On the shell this multiplier
is $-\omega_\mu(\mathbf k)^2+|\mathbf k|^2+\mu^2=0$. Restriction to the
shell therefore gives the asserted Klein–Gordon identity.

An **oriented time-oriented affine Minkowski space** is a quadruple
$(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ with the following data. In this notation $V$ includes its
specified orientation; forgetting that orientation gives only the underlying
real vector space, not the full datum $V$ of the model.

1. A nonempty affine space $A$ over a $4$-dimensional real vector space $V$,
   with action $(p,v)\mapsto p+v$ and displacement $q-p\in V$
   ([[def-affine-space-and-displacement]]). In particular $V$ is a real vector
   space of dimension $4$.
2. A Lorentz form $\eta$ on $V$, i.e. a nondegenerate symmetric bilinear form of
   inertia $(3,1,0)$ ([[def-lorentz-form-and-inertia]]). Its associated quadratic
   form is $q(v)=\eta(v,v)$.
3. An **orientation** of $V$: a positive ray of the determinant line
   $\Lambda^4V$, fixed once and for all
   ([[def-determinant-line-orientation-of-a-finite-dimensional-real-vector-space]]).
4. A **time orientation** $C^+$ of $(V,\eta)$: one of the two connected
   components of the timelike set $T=\{v\in V:\eta(v,v)<0\}$, the other being
   $C^-:=T\setminus C^+$ ([[def-time-orientation-and-future-causal-sets]]).

The following terminology is attached to such a quadruple.

- The elements $p$ of $A$ are the **events**; for events $p,q$ the vector
  $q-p\in V$ is the **displacement from $p$ to $q$**.
- The **interval** of $p,q\in A$ is the real number
  $I(p,q):=\eta(q-p,q-p)=q(q-p)$.
- Events $p,q$ are **timelike**, **null**, **spacelike** or **causally
  related** when the displacement $q-p$ is timelike, null, spacelike or causal
  in the sense of [[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]]; they are
  **future-related** when $q-p$ is future causal and **past-related** when
  $q-p$ is past causal in the sense of
  [[def-time-orientation-and-future-causal-sets]].

**No point of $A$ is distinguished.** For every $v\in V$ the translation
$\tau_v:A\to A$, $\tau_v(p):=p+v$, is a bijection, since it is inverse to
$\tau_{-v}$: $\tau_{-v}(\tau_v(p))=(p+v)+(-v)=p+(v-v)=p$ and symmetrically, by
the affine action axioms ([[def-affine-space-and-displacement]]). Displacements
are translation invariant, $\tau_v(q)-\tau_v(p)=q-p$, so every $\tau_v$ preserves
the interval, the causal classification of every ordered pair, and the sets
$C^+$, $C^-$ (which are subsets of $V$, independent of the point of $A$); it
changes only the labelling of points. The mathematical structure of the model is
exactly the quadruple $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$; no derived physical quantity (proper
time, four-velocity, momentum, energy, charge or any field) is part of this
definition, and all later structure of the framework (frames, charts, tensor
fields, worldlines) is built on this model.

**Well-definedness.** The affine-space definition supplies the action and the
unique displacements; the Lorentz-form definition supplies $\eta$ and its
inertia; the determinant-line definition supplies orientations; and the two
components of $T$ between which the time-orientation definition chooses exist by
the components lemma recorded in the well-definedness clause of
[[def-time-orientation-and-future-causal-sets]], which is also what makes the
names future and past causal in item 4 well defined.

Let $V$ be a $4$-dimensional real vector space ([[def-vector-space]],
[[def-dimension]]). A **Lorentz form** on $V$ is a symmetric bilinear form
$\eta:V\times V\to\mathbb R$ ([[def-bilinear-symmetric-skew-and-alternating-forms]])
such that

1. $\eta$ is nondegenerate: both radicals
   $\operatorname{rad}_L(\eta)=\{u:\eta(u,v)=0\text{ for every }v\}$ and
   $\operatorname{rad}_R(\eta)=\{v:\eta(u,v)=0\text{ for every }u\}$ are
   $\{0\}$ ([[def-matrix-radicals-rank-and-nondegeneracy-of-a-bilinear-form]]);
   and
2. $\eta$ has **inertia** $(3,1,0)$: in some (equivalently, in every) basis of
   $V$ in which the matrix of $\eta$ is diagonal, exactly three diagonal
   entries are positive, exactly one is negative, and none is zero
   ([[def-definiteness-inertia-and-signature-data-over-the-reals]]).

The inertia of a symmetric bilinear form is the triple $(p,q,r)$ of numbers of
positive, negative and zero diagonal entries of any diagonalizing basis, and it
is independent of the diagonalizing basis by Sylvester's law of inertia
([[def-definiteness-inertia-and-signature-data-over-the-reals]]); hence clause 2
is a property of $\eta$ itself and not of a chosen basis. The **associated
quadratic form** of $\eta$ is

$$q(v):=\eta(v,v),\qquad v\in V .$$

A **Lorentz vector space of signature $(-,+,+,+)$** is a pair $(V,\eta)$
consisting of a $4$-dimensional real vector space $V$ and a Lorentz form $\eta$
on $V$; the name records that the diagonal normal form of $\eta$ has one
negative entry followed by three positive entries. No positive-definite
structure on $V$ is assumed or implied by this definition, and $q$ takes both
negative and positive values on nonzero vectors: a basis in which
$\eta$ is diagonal with diagonal entries $-1,1,1,1$ exists by clause 2, and on
its first vector $q$ is $-1$, while on each of the other three it is $+1$.

Let $(V,\eta)$ be a Lorentz vector space of signature $(-,+,+,+)$
([[def-lorentz-form-and-inertia]]), with causal terminology as in
[[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]], and let

$$T:=\{v\in V:\eta(v,v)<0\}$$

be its **timelike set**. Components and closures refer to the topology obtained
by using any ordered basis to identify $V$ with Euclidean $\mathbb R^4$;
[[lem-timelike-cone-has-two-convex-components]], step 5.1, proves that the
resulting open sets are independent of the basis. By that lemma the
set $T$ has exactly two connected components, and each of them is nonempty,
open, convex and path-connected. A **time orientation** of $(V,\eta)$ is a
choice of one of these two components. Fixing such a choice, write $C^+$ for the
chosen component and

$$C^-:=T\setminus C^+$$

for the other component; thus $T=C^+\sqcup C^-$ is a disjoint union and
$C^+$, $C^-$ are exactly the two components supplied by the lemma. Relative to
this choice a vector $v\in V$ is

- **future timelike** when $v\in C^+$;
- **past timelike** when $v\in C^-$;
- **future null** when $v\neq 0$, $\eta(v,v)=0$ and $v\in\operatorname{cl}(C^+)$;
- **past null** when $v\neq 0$, $\eta(v,v)=0$ and $v\in\operatorname{cl}(C^-)$;
- **future causal** when it is future timelike or future null;
- **past causal** when it is past timelike or past null.

The sets $\operatorname{cl}(C^+)$ and $\operatorname{cl}(C^-)$ are the
**future closed cone** and the **past closed cone** of the time-oriented space
$(V,\eta,C^+)$. By [[lem-timelike-cone-has-two-convex-components]] each of them
is a convex cone, their intersection is $\{0\}$, and a vector is causal exactly
when it is future causal or past causal, in which case exactly one of these two
alternatives holds: no nonzero vector is both future causal and past causal.
The timelike vectors are exactly the points of $T=C^+\cup C^-$, and
$0\notin T$ because $\eta(0,0)=0$; since a null vector is nonzero with
$\eta(v,v)=0$, no vector is both timelike and null, so the classes above are
mutually exclusive where the definitions say they are: no vector is both future
and past causal, and no timelike vector is null.

$$D(g\circ f)(a)=Dg(f(a))\circ Df(a).$$

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let
$U,V \subseteq \mathbb R^n$ be open and let $T : U \to V$ be a
$C^1$ diffeomorphism. For every nonnegative Lebesgue measurable
$f : V \to [0,\infty]$,
$$ \int_V f(y)\,d\lambda_n(y) = \int_U f(T(x))\,|\det DT(x)|\,d\lambda_n(x). $$

$f_n\to f$ almost everywhere and $|f_n|\le g$ almost everywhere for a single
nonnegative measurable function $g$ with $\int g\,d\mu<+\infty$. Then
$f\in L^1(\mu)$,
$$\int|f_n-f|\,d\mu\longrightarrow0,$$
and hence
$$\int f_n\,d\mu\longrightarrow\int f\,d\mu.$$

space. Repeated chain rule [F6] expresses each derivative as a finite linear
combination of derivatives of $f$ at $\Lambda^{-1}(x-a)$. Also

preserves null-equivalence classes for the same reason. Therefore $U_\mu(g)$
is a well-defined isometry. Its inverse is the corresponding formula for
$g^{-1}$, so it is unitary. Direct substitution and Lorentz invariance of

$U_\mu(a,\Lambda)U_\mu(b,\Gamma)
=U_\mu(a+\Lambda b,\Lambda\Gamma)$.

$$K_\mu f_g(p)=e^{ip\circ a}K_\mu f(\Lambda^{-1}p).$$
Both sides belong to $H_\mu$ by [F4], so this equality is also equality of
Hilbert-space vectors. This is the action formula used in step 1.2.

family. Density follows from [F3]. For arbitrary $v\in H_\mu$, choose such

$$\|U_\mu(g)v-U_\mu(g_0)v\| \le2\epsilon+\|U_\mu(g)h-U_\mu(g_0)h\|.$$

continuity on all of $H_\mu$.
