$W_{\rm Segal}$ is the unitary generated by the closed Segal field, with the
normalization and phase convention of
[[lem-qft-smeared-free-scalar]]. Define the scalar bounded observable algebra
$\mathfrak A_s(O)$ to be the norm closure of the unital $*$-algebra generated
by these $W_\mu(f)$. The real smeared field is symmetric on
$\mathcal D_{\rm fin}$ and its self-adjoint closure has the exact multiplier
domain supplied by [[lem-qft-free-domain-observables]] and
[[lem-qft-segal-weyl-domain]].

For Dirac tests, $\Psi(F)$ is the bounded smeared CAR field of
[[lem-qft-free-dirac-car-locality]]. Define $\mathfrak A_D(O)$ as the norm
closure of the unital algebra generated by products containing an even number
of these field operators and their adjoints, with all test supports in $O$.
“Even” here means even field parity, or equivalently an even number of odd
CAR field generators in each product. The even algebra is the selected local
Dirac observable algebra; an odd charged field is not included as a commuting
local observable.

The selected vacuum states on bounded operators are the vector states
$\omega_s(A)=\langle\Omega_s,A\Omega_s\rangle$ and
$\omega_D(B)=\langle\Omega_D,B\Omega_D\rangle$. For the scalar Fock space,
define the total number, Hamiltonian, and translation momentum components by
$$N_s=d\Gamma_s(1),\qquad H_s=\hbar c\,d\Gamma_s(\omega_\mu),\qquad P_{s,j}=\hbar\,d\Gamma_s(-k_j).$$
Here $d\Gamma_s$ acts on the $n$-particle sector by summing the displayed
one-particle multiplier over its $n$ arguments. Their maximal domains are
the square-integrability domains of those sector sums; in particular,
$$D(N_s)=\left\{\Psi=(\Psi_n):\sum_{n\ge1}n^2\|\Psi_n\|^2<\infty\right\}.$$
The sign in $P_{s,j}$ matches the field translation phase
$\omega_\mu x^0-\mathbf k\cdot\mathbf x$. For the Dirac Fock space, let $H$
and $P_j$ be the mathematical translation generators of
[[lem-qft-dirac-fermionic-translation-spectrum]]. Their one-particle
multipliers are respectively $(\omega_\mu,\mathbf k)$ for particles and
$(\omega_\mu,-\mathbf k)$ for antiparticles, and the sector multiplier is
their sum. Define the physical Dirac Hamiltonian and momentum by
$H_D=\hbar cH$ and $P_{D,j}=\hbar P_j$, using the positive SI constants from
[[def-qft-framework-units]]. Their exact domains are unchanged by these
nonzero scale factors; their multipliers have units joules and momentum,
respectively.

For any of these self-adjoint operators $A$, a normalized state
$\Psi\in D(A)$ has model mean $\langle\Psi,A\Psi\rangle$ and variance
$\operatorname{Var}_\Psi(A)=\|(A-\langle\Psi,A\Psi\rangle)\Psi\|^2$.
This requires the second spectral moment but does not require
$\Psi\in D(A^2)$. Products of unbounded operators use their composition
domains.

If a signed charge parameter $q_{\rm SI}\in\mathbb R$ measured in coulombs is supplied, the intended
Dirac charge-number operator is $Q_{\rm SI}=q_{\rm SI}(N_p-N_{\bar p})$.
Here $\Pi_p$ and $\Pi_{\bar p}$ are the orthogonal projections onto
$\mathcal H_+$ and $\overline{\mathcal H_-}$; on the $n$-particle sector,
$N_p$ and $N_{\bar p}$ are the sums of the corresponding projections over
the $n$ tensor factors. Its candidate maximal direct-sum domain is
$$D(Q_{\rm SI})=\left\{\Psi=(\Psi_n):\sum_{n\ge0}\left\|q_{\rm SI}\sum_{r=1}^n(\Pi_p-\Pi_{\bar p})^{(r)}\Psi_n\right\|^2<\infty\right\}.$$
This is a candidate definition only; no self-adjointness or proved-domain
claim is asserted here.

Measurements in this model are assigned only when a state and a normalized
finite bounded Kraus instrument have actually been constructed. For such an
instrument, the adopted outcome probabilities and positive-probability
conditional states are exactly those of
[[post-qft-constructed-model-and-measurement]]. They are model probabilities,
not observed outcomes. The field definitions are test-smeared: neither
$\Phi_\mu(x)$ nor $\Psi(x)$ is a pointwise operator supplied here, and the
smearing results do not define coincident products or a diagonal restriction.

supplier_excerpts.exact_statement:
Assume Countable Choice [[def-countable-choice]].
Let $O\subseteq\mathbb R^4$ be open. For real
$f\in C_c^\infty(O)$ define
$$W_\mu(f):=W_{\rm Segal}(\sqrt2K_\mu f),$$
where the Segal normalization is exactly
$\Phi_{\rm Segal}(h)=(a^\dagger(h)+a(h))/\sqrt2$ on the finite-particle
domain, as in [[lem-qft-segal-weyl-domain]]. This scale makes the generator
of $t\mapsto W_\mu(tf)$ equal to the real scalar field
$\Phi_\mu(f)=a(K_\mu f)+a^\dagger(K_\mu f)$ of
[[lem-qft-smeared-free-scalar]]. Define the unital norm-closed operator
algebra
$$\mathfrak A_\mu(O)= \overline{\operatorname{alg}}^{\|\cdot\|} \{I,W_\mu(f),W_\mu(f)^*:f\in C_c^\infty(O;\mathbb R)\}.$$
Then $O_1\subseteq O_2$ implies
$\mathfrak A_\mu(O_1)\subseteq\mathfrak A_\mu(O_2)$. If every difference
$x-y$, with $x\in O_1$ and $y\in O_2$, is spacelike, then every element of
$\mathfrak A_\mu(O_1)$ commutes with every element of
$\mathfrak A_\mu(O_2)$. These are algebraic properties of the constructed
representation; they are not empirical signaling or measurement claims.

supplier_excerpts.exact_statement:
Assume Countable Choice [[def-countable-choice]], let $\mu\ge0$, and use [[def-qft-dirac-projections]], [[lem-qft-dirac-projection-matrices]], and the antisymmetric Fock and CAR conventions of [[def-qft-fock-and-test-spaces]] and [[lem-qft-fock-ccr-car]]. For $F\in\mathscr S(\mathbb R^4;\mathbb C^4)$, define
$$\widehat F(t,\mathbf k)=\int_{\mathbb R^3}e^{-i\mathbf k\cdot\mathbf x}F(t,\mathbf x)\,d^3\mathbf x,\qquad u_F(\mathbf k)=\int_{\mathbb R}W_D(t,\mathbf k)\widehat F(t,\mathbf k)\,dt.$$
Then $u_F\in\mathcal H_D$, continuously in the Schwartz topology, and
$$\Psi(F)=c(P_+u_F)+c^\dagger(\overline{P_-u_F})$$
defines a bounded operator on $\mathcal F_a(\mathcal H_+\oplus\overline{\mathcal H_-})$, antilinear in $F$. It satisfies
$$\{\Psi(F),\Psi(G)\}=0,\qquad \{\Psi(F),\Psi(G)^\dagger\}=\langle u_F,u_G\rangle_{\mathcal H_D}I.$$
The positive and negative contraction kernels, defined as tempered distributions by their Fourier integrals, are
$$C_+(\tau,\mathbf x)=\int e^{-i(\omega\tau-\mathbf k\cdot\mathbf x)}P_+(\mathbf k)\,\frac{d^3\mathbf k}{(2\pi)^3},\qquad C_-(\tau,\mathbf x)=\int e^{+i(\omega\tau+\mathbf k\cdot\mathbf x)}P_-(\mathbf k)\,\frac{d^3\mathbf k}{(2\pi)^3}.$$
Their tested pairings give respectively $\langle P_+u_F,P_+u_G\rangle$ and $\langle P_-u_F,P_-u_G\rangle$; their sum is the anticommutator kernel $R$ below.
Its tested free equation is $u_{(i\partial_0-h_D(-i\nabla))F}=0$. For spatial Schwartz spinors $u,v$, the equal-time field $\Psi_t(u)=c(P_+W_D(t,\mathbf k)\widehat u)+c^\dagger(\overline{P_-W_D(t,\mathbf k)\widehat u})$ satisfies $\{\Psi_t(u),\Psi_t(v)^\dagger\}=\int u(\mathbf x)^\dagger v(\mathbf x)\,d^3\mathbf x\,I$ and $\{\Psi_t(u),\Psi_t(v)\}=0$.

The spacetime anticommutator kernel is
$$R(\tau,\mathbf x)=\int_{\mathbb R^3}W_D(-\tau,\mathbf k)e^{i\mathbf k\cdot\mathbf x}\,\frac{d^3\mathbf k}{(2\pi)^3}=\partial_\tau\Delta_\mu(\tau,\mathbf x)I_4-i h_D(-i\nabla)\Delta_\mu(\tau,\mathbf x),$$
where $\Delta_\mu$ is the scalar causal commutator distribution of [[lem-qft-scalar-causal-commutator]]. Thus the kernel is supported in the closed causal cone. Spinor tests with compact spacelike-separated supports have vanishing anticommutators with one another and with each other's adjoints. Consequently, even polynomials in the bounded smeared fields commute across spacelike-separated regions. These are mathematical properties of the specified free-field construction.

supplier_excerpts.exact_statement:
Let $f$ and $(f_n)$ be measurable complex-valued functions such that
$f_n\to f$ almost everywhere and $|f_n|\le g$ almost everywhere for a single
nonnegative measurable function $g$ with $\int g\,d\mu<+\infty$. Then
$f\in L^1(\mu)$,
$$\int|f_n-f|\,d\mu\longrightarrow0,$$
and hence
$$\int f_n\,d\mu\longrightarrow\int f\,d\mu.$$

derivations.claim:
The adopted physical systems are exactly the two selected Fock
representations in [F2], and [F1] fixes the spacetime and unit convention.
The test spaces and meanings of $\mathfrak A_s(O)$ and $\mathfrak A_D(O)$ are
those defined in [F4]; thus all fields used here are smeared and all Dirac
local observables are even products.

Apply [F6] to the listed real scalar smearings and sector-sum generators.
It supplies their exact maximal domains and, for every normalized
$\Psi\in D(A)$, finite $\langle\Psi,A\Psi\rangle$ and finite variance.
The same statement gives the product-domain condition, so no claim about
$D(A^2)$ or an everywhere-defined product follows.

The region hypotheses in the Statement are exactly the spacelike-support
hypotheses of [F8] and [F10]. The first gives commutativity of the scalar
Weyl algebras; the second gives commutativity of the bounded even Dirac local
algebras. If either region is empty, its test space is $\{0\}$ and
its unital generated algebra is $\mathbb C I$, which commutes with the other
algebra as well.

For every Schwartz $g$, changing variables gives
$\int\rho_{\epsilon,x_0}(x)g(x)\,d^4x=
\int\rho(y)g(x_0+\epsilon y)\,d^4y\to g(x_0)$ by dominated convergence [F11].
For every spatial Schwartz spinor $h$, the corresponding pairing is
$$\int u_{\epsilon,x_0}(\mathbf x)^\dagger h(\mathbf x)\,d^3\mathbf x=
\int\sigma(y)z^\dagger h(\mathbf x_0+\epsilon y)\,d^3y
\longrightarrow z^\dagger h(\mathbf x_0),$$
again by dominated convergence with the integrable bound
$\|h\|_\infty\sigma(y)$ [F11]. The equal-time Dirac operator in this family
is the $\Psi_t(u)$ of [F9].
The actual current proof of [F7] gives diverging scalar vacuum-vector norms
and equal-time Dirac operator norms for these Gaussian families. A norm-convergent vector or bounded-operator family
must have bounded norms, so neither family has such a limit.

The selected definition [F5] supplies no other point field or diagonal
product. The norm obstruction in step 1.4 is specific to the displayed
representations and topologies.

When the state and finite instrument required by [F3] are supplied, the
Born postulate assigns the stated model probabilities. No such state,
instrument, apparatus, or observation is introduced by this theorem, so it
establishes no empirical outcome.

citations.quote:
The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

Fix the oriented, time-oriented affine Minkowski spacetime and an inertial
chart of [[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]] and
[[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]]. Use signature
$\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, length coordinates
$x^0=ct$ and $x^i$ in metres, and coordinate time $t$ in seconds as in
[[def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions]]. Greek spacetime indices run
from $0$ to $3$; spatial indices run from $1$ to $3$ and are contracted with
the Euclidean spatial metric. The coordinates $x^a$ have unit metre and
$\partial_a:=\partial/\partial x^a$ has unit $\mathrm m^{-1}$.

The positive constants $c$, $h$ and $e_{\rm SI}$ have the exact SI defining
values; write $\hbar:=h/(2\pi)$. The magnetic constant $\mu_0>0$ has SI unit
$\mathrm{N\,A^{-2}}$ and is experimentally determined under the current SI;
no exact numerical value or current estimate for it is adopted. Put
$\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$ when that symbol is used. These are SI
normalization inputs, not empirical claims about a selected QFT model.

For a species with rest mass $m_{\rm rest,SI}>0$ in kilograms define its
inverse-length mass parameter

$$\mu:=\frac{m_{\rm rest,SI}c}{\hbar}\quad[\mathrm m^{-1}].$$

For spatial wave vector $\mathbf k$ in $\mathrm m^{-1}$ put
$\omega(\mathbf k):=\sqrt{|\mathbf k|^2+\mu^2}$ in $\mathrm m^{-1}$. Here
$\omega$ is the temporal wave number, not the SI angular frequency; the
corresponding SI angular frequency is $c\omega$. Energy and momentum are
$E=\hbar c\omega$ in joules and $\mathbf p=\hbar\mathbf k$ in
$\mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-1}}$. With $p=(\omega,\mathbf k)$ the phase convention is

$$p\mathbin{\circ}x:=\omega x^0-\mathbf k\cdot\mathbf x=-\eta(p,x).$$

The natural action is $S/\hbar$. Its canonical density in four dimensions has
unit $\mathrm m^{-4}$; the corresponding physical energy density is
$\hbar c$ times that density and has unit $\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}}$.

For canonical engineering dimensions in this four-dimensional normalization,
write $\phi_{\rm n}$ for a scalar field with length degree $-1$ and
$\psi_{\rm n}$ for a Dirac field with length degree $-3/2$. These are the
dimensions fixed by the selected free kinetic terms, not exact scaling
dimensions of interacting fields: anomalous dimensions, when present, are
separate quantities. Let $A^\mu_{\rm SI}=(\varphi/c,\mathbf A)$ and
$F^{\mu\nu}_{\rm SI}$ use the component convention of
[[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]], namely
$F_{0i}=-E_i/c$ and $F_{ij}=\epsilon_{ijk}B_k$, with
$F_{\mu\nu}=\partial_\mu A_\nu-\partial_\nu A_\mu$ only when a potential is
supplied. Define the normalized photon potential and field strength by

$$a^\mu:=\frac{A^\mu_{\rm SI}}{\sqrt{\mu_0\hbar c}},\qquad
f^{\mu\nu}:=\frac{F^{\mu\nu}_{\rm SI}}{\sqrt{\mu_0\hbar c}}.$$

They have length degrees $-1$ and $-2$, respectively. The EM supplier is used
only for SI units and tensor components: no classical Maxwell equation,
Lorentz-force law, or classical-to-quantum identification is adopted here.

For any separately declared SI charge parameter $q_{\rm SI}$ in coulombs put

$$q_{\rm n}:=q_{\rm SI}\sqrt{\frac{\mu_0c}{\hbar}}.$$

It is dimensionless. For the positive exact SI elementary charge use
$e_{\rm n}:=e_{\rm SI}\sqrt{\mu_0c/\hbar}$ and define the rationalized
dimensionless coupling $\alpha:=e_{\rm n}^2/(4\pi)$. Since $\mu_0$ is
measured, these formulas do not assign an exact numerical value to
$e_{\rm n}$ or $\alpha$. If the model uses minimal coupling, its convention is
$D_\mu=\partial_\mu-iq_{\rm n}a_\mu$; for an electron with
$q_{\rm SI}=-e_{\rm SI}$ this reads $D_\mu=\partial_\mu+ie_{\rm n}a_\mu$.
Bare, renormalized-at-scale, and measured effective charges are separately
labelled model parameters; applying the conversion to one label does not
identify it with either of the others or specify a running law.

The Clifford convention is $\gamma^0=\beta$, $\gamma^i=\beta\alpha^i$,
$\{\gamma^a,\gamma^b\}=-2\eta^{ab}$, so the effective Clifford metric is
$-\eta$. In a supplied free Dirac model the displayed equation is
$(i\gamma^a\partial_a-\mu)\psi=0$. The phase and Clifford choices are
conventions; this item proves no Dirac representation or field equation.
Time evolution is written $U(t)=\exp(-itH/\hbar)$ when a selected model has
actually constructed a self-adjoint Hamiltonian $H$ and its unitary group; the
corresponding Heisenberg conjugation is $O_H(t)=U(t)^*O\,U(t)$. No such
Hamiltonian or group is constructed here. Where a free-field module uses an
inner product linear in its second variable, convert to the repository's
first-variable-linear pairing by
$\langle u,v\rangle_{\rm FF}=(v,u)_{\rm root}$.

For precision about domains, let $\mathcal H$ be a complex Hilbert space with
inner product linear in its first variable and let
$\mathscr D\subseteq\mathcal H$ be a dense complex linear subspace. A **weak operator-valued distribution
on the common domain $\mathscr D$** means a complex-linear assignment
$g\mapsto\Phi(g)$ for $g\in\mathcal D(\mathbb R^4)$, where each
$\Phi(g):\mathscr D\to\mathcal H$ is linear and, for every
$u,v\in\mathscr D$, the scalar map
$g\mapsto\langle\Phi(g)u,v\rangle$ is a continuous complex-linear functional
on the test-function space with the topology of
[[def-test-function-topology]], hence a distribution as in [[def-distribution]].
This definition gives no pointwise field $\Phi(x)$ and no product
$\Phi(x)\Phi(x)$; a product or extension needs a separate construction.
Smeared fields are not thereby bounded, symmetric, self-adjoint, or
self-adjointly closable. Locality, local observable algebras, graded locality,
and gauge-specific potential behavior are likewise supplied only by the
relevant constructed model modules. Test-function units can be chosen so a
specified smeared observable is dimensionless; there is no universal test
function unit asserted here.

Primitive data for a selected model include its species and rest masses,
declared charge parameters, regulator geometry, couplings, state and any
constructed measurement data. Vacuum-subtracted Hamiltonians, regulator
eigenvalues, distributions, correlations and outcome probabilities are
derived only when their constructions supply the required domains and
well-definedness. This dictionary neither constructs an interacting
four-dimensional QED Hilbert space nor asserts pointwise field products,
scattering, an LSZ limit, asymptotic completeness, or removal of a regulator.

Fix four-dimensional affine Minkowski spacetime with metric
$\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, an inertial length-coordinate chart
$x=(x^0,\mathbf x)$, $x^0=ct$, and coordinates measured in metres, as specified
by [[def-qft-framework-units]]. Write
$\Box=\eta^{ab}\partial_a\partial_b$. The mass-shell parameter $\mu\ge0$ has
unit $\mathrm m^{-1}$ and
$\omega_\mu(\mathbf k)=\sqrt{|\mathbf k|^2+\mu^2}$ has the same unit. For a
massive species, $\mu=m_{\mathrm{rest,SI}}c/\hbar$; $\mu=0$ is the separately
admitted massless branch of the mathematical free-field construction. Thus
$\hbar c\omega_\mu$ is physical energy and $\hbar\mathbf k$ is physical
momentum. The natural-unit action is written $S/\hbar$.

The scalar one-particle space is
$\mathcal H_\mu=L^2(H_\mu^+,d\nu_\mu;\mathbb C)$, where
$H_\mu^+=\{(\omega_\mu(\mathbf k),\mathbf k):\mathbf k\in\mathbb R^3,\ \omega_\mu(\mathbf k)>0\}$ and
$d\nu_\mu=d^3\mathbf k/((2\pi)^3\,2\omega_\mu(\mathbf k))$; at $\mu=0$ the
measure-zero apex $\mathbf k=0$ is omitted. These are the shell conventions
of [[lem-qft-smeared-free-scalar]].

For a smooth real classical scalar $\phi_{\mathrm n}:\mathbb R^4\to\mathbb R$
with the canonical free-field length degree $-1$, adopt
$$\frac{S_\phi}{\hbar}=-\frac12\int_{\mathbb R^4}\left(\eta^{ab}\partial_a\phi_{\mathrm n}\partial_b\phi_{\mathrm n}+\mu^2\phi_{\mathrm n}^2\right)\,d^4x.$$
For a smooth commuting classical Dirac spinor
$\psi_{\mathrm n}:\mathbb R^4\to\mathbb C^4$ with canonical free-field length
degree $-3/2$, put $\bar\psi_{\mathrm n}=\psi_{\mathrm n}^\dagger\beta$ and
use the Clifford convention
$\{\gamma^a,\gamma^b\}=-2\eta^{ab}I_4$ from
[[def-qft-framework-units]]. Adopt
$$\frac{S_D}{\hbar}=\int_{\mathbb R^4}\bar\psi_{\mathrm n}(i\gamma^a\partial_a-\mu)\psi_{\mathrm n}\,d^4x.$$
The smooth classical variables in these functionals commute; no Grassmann
algebra or path-integral construction is being adopted. These formulas specify
local action densities: for arbitrary smooth global fields the total
integrals need not converge. Only compactly supported variations are used;
the action difference under such a variation is an integral over a compact
set and is finite for smooth fields. With these variations on the fixed
background, the intended Euler–Lagrange equations are
$(\Box-\mu^2)\phi_{\mathrm n}=0$ and
$(i\gamma^a\partial_a-\mu)\psi_{\mathrm n}=0$, conditional on the exact

supplier_excerpts.exact_statement:
The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

$\mathcal D_{\rm fin}\to\mathcal D_{\rm fin}$. For real $f$ it is symmetric
and equals $\sqrt2\,\Phi_{\rm Segal}(K_\mu f)|_{\mathcal D_{\rm fin}}$, where the Segal field of

$\Phi_{\rm Segal}(h)=\overline{(a^\dagger(h)+a(h))/\sqrt2}$.

$W_\mu(f):=W_{\rm Segal}(\sqrt2 K_\mu f)$ and, for real $f,g$,
$$W_\mu(f)W_\mu(g)= e^{-i\,\operatorname{Im}\langle K_\mu f,K_\mu g\rangle_2}W_\mu(f+g).$$
For every real $f$ the vacuum Weyl expectation is
$$\langle\Omega,W_\mu(f)\Omega\rangle_2 =e^{-\|K_\mu f\|_2^2/2}.$$
Here the inner product is second-variable-linear as fixed in
[[def-qft-fock-and-test-spaces]]. The vacuum has zero one-point function and
two-point function
$$\langle\Omega,\Phi_\mu(f)\Phi_\mu(g)\Omega\rangle_2 =\langle K_\mu\overline f,K_\mu g\rangle_2,$$
which obeys $\langle\Omega,\Phi_\mu(\overline f)\Phi_\mu(f)\Omega\rangle_2=\|K_\mu f\|_2^2\ge0$ for every complex test $f$ (ordinary diagonal positivity holds for real tests); higher vacuum moments of ordered real smeared
fields obey the CCR pairing recursion and hence the free-field Wick pairing
rule. $$W_\mu(z)=\int_{H_\mu^+}e^{-ip\circ z}\,d\nu_\mu(p),$$

second-quantized multiplier measure with one-particle vector

future cone $\{(E,\mathbf P):E\ge|\mathbf P|\}$; the vacuum is an eigenvector
at $(0,\mathbf0)$. These are conditional mathematical model deductions.

Assume Countable Choice [[def-countable-choice]], let $\mu\ge0$, and use [[def-qft-dirac-projections]], [[lem-qft-dirac-projection-matrices]], and the antisymmetric Fock and CAR conventions of [[def-qft-fock-and-test-spaces]] and [[lem-qft-fock-ccr-car]]. For $F\in\mathscr S(\mathbb R^4;\mathbb C^4)$, define
$$\widehat F(t,\mathbf k)=\int_{\mathbb R^3}e^{-i\mathbf k\cdot\mathbf x}F(t,\mathbf x)\,d^3\mathbf x,\qquad u_F(\mathbf k)=\int_{\mathbb R}W_D(t,\mathbf k)\widehat F(t,\mathbf k)\,dt.$$
Then $u_F\in\mathcal H_D$, continuously in the Schwartz topology, and
$$\Psi(F)=c(P_+u_F)+c^\dagger(\overline{P_-u_F})$$
defines a bounded operator on $\mathcal F_a(\mathcal H_+\oplus\overline{\mathcal H_-})$, antilinear in $F$. It satisfies
$$\{\Psi(F),\Psi(G)\}=0,\qquad \{\Psi(F),\Psi(G)^\dagger\}=\langle u_F,u_G\rangle_{\mathcal H_D}I.$$
The positive and negative contraction kernels, defined as tempered distributions by their Fourier integrals, are
$$C_+(\tau,\mathbf x)=\int e^{-i(\omega\tau-\mathbf k\cdot\mathbf x)}P_+(\mathbf k)\,\frac{d^3\mathbf k}{(2\pi)^3},\qquad C_-(\tau,\mathbf x)=\int e^{+i(\omega\tau+\mathbf k\cdot\mathbf x)}P_-(\mathbf k)\,\frac{d^3\mathbf k}{(2\pi)^3}.$$
Their tested pairings give respectively $\langle P_+u_F,P_+u_G\rangle$ and $\langle P_-u_F,P_-u_G\rangle$; their sum is the anticommutator kernel $R$ below.
Its tested free equation is $u_{(i\partial_0-h_D(-i\nabla))F}=0$. For spatial Schwartz spinors $u,v$, the equal-time field $\Psi_t(u)=c(P_+W_D(t,\mathbf k)\widehat u)+c^\dagger(\overline{P_-W_D(t,\mathbf k)\widehat u})$ satisfies $\{\Psi_t(u),\Psi_t(v)^\dagger\}=\int u(\mathbf x)^\dagger v(\mathbf x)\,d^3\mathbf x\,I$ and $\{\Psi_t(u),\Psi_t(v)\}=0$.

The spacetime anticommutator kernel is
$$R(\tau,\mathbf x)=\int_{\mathbb R^3}W_D(-\tau,\mathbf k)e^{i\mathbf k\cdot\mathbf x}\,\frac{d^3\mathbf k}{(2\pi)^3}=\partial_\tau\Delta_\mu(\tau,\mathbf x)I_4-i h_D(-i\nabla)\Delta_\mu(\tau,\mathbf x),$$
where $\Delta_\mu$ is the scalar causal commutator distribution of [[lem-qft-scalar-causal-commutator]]. Thus the kernel is supported in the closed causal cone. Spinor tests with compact spacelike-separated supports have vanishing anticommutators with one another and with each other's adjoints. Consequently, even polynomials in the bounded smeared fields commute across spacelike-separated regions. These are mathematical properties of the specified free-field construction.

By [F3], for each compactly supported smooth real variation $h$ and
compactly supported smooth spinor variation $\chi$, the first variations of
the displayed actions are the stated integrals against
$(\Box-\mu^2)\phi_{\mathrm n}$ and
$(i\gamma^a\partial_a-\mu)\psi_{\mathrm n}$. The lemma proves both
necessity and sufficiency of the displayed pointwise equations for
stationarity under all such variations; this step uses the commuting
classical spinor convention of [F2].

Since $\Box-\mu^2=-(\partial_0^2-\Delta+\mu^2)$, [F4] and linearity
give $K_\mu((\Box-\mu^2)f)=0$ for every Schwartz $f$. The differential
operator has real coefficients, so the same identity holds for $\overline f$.
The scalar field formula in [F5] applies $a$ and $a^\dagger$ only to
$K_\mu\overline f$ and $K_\mu f$; both vanish for $f$ replaced by
$(\Box-\mu^2)f$. Hence the constructed scalar field satisfies the stated
weak test equation.

By [F7], the one-particle vector of
$(i\partial_0-h_D(-i\nabla))F$ is zero. Substitution in the bounded CAR
field formula in [F6] makes both its creation and annihilation terms zero,
so the corresponding smeared field is zero. From [F2],
$$\beta(i\partial_0-h_D(-i\nabla))
=i\beta\partial_0+i\beta\alpha^j\partial_j-\mu
=i\gamma^a\partial_a-\mu,$$
using $\beta^2=I_4$. Thus this is exactly the tested Dirac differential
expression in the classical equation of [F3].

the physical adoption [F2]; steps 1.1–1.3 establish equation agreement under

free model and carries no empirical or general quantization claim.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Fix the scalar shell parameter $\mu\ge0$ and all shell, Fourier, and metric conventions of [[def-qft-scalar-mass-shell]], with $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$ and $\Box=-\partial_t^2+\Delta_{\mathbf x}$. For $\phi\in\mathcal S(\mathbb R^4)$ define the partial spatial Fourier transform
$$\widehat\phi_t(\mathbf k)=\int_{\mathbb R^3}e^{-i\mathbf k\cdot\mathbf x}\phi(t,\mathbf x)\,d^3\mathbf x$$
and define $H_\mu\in\mathcal S'(\mathbb R^4)$ by
$$\langle H_\mu,\phi\rangle=\int_{\mathbb R}dt\int_{\mathbb R^3}\frac{d^3\mathbf k}{(2\pi)^3\,2\omega_\mu(\mathbf k)}e^{-i\omega_\mu(\mathbf k)|t|}\widehat\phi_t(-\mathbf k).$$
This is a continuous distributional extension of the free scalar time-ordered two-point function: on $t>0$ its kernel is the Wightman two-point distribution $W_\mu(t,\mathbf x)$, and on $t<0$ it is $W_\mu(-t,-\mathbf x)$. The displayed partial Fourier formula fixes the extension at $t=0$; no product of a step function with an unspecified singular distribution is used. The kernel is symmetric under $(t,\mathbf x)\mapsto(-t,-\mathbf x)$, agrees with the two orderings on spacelike-separated supports, and obeys
$$ (\Box-\mu^2)H_\mu=i\delta_0 $$
in $\mathcal S'(\mathbb R^4)$. There is no extra prefactor $i$ in the definition of $H_\mu$.

Assume Countable Choice [[def-countable-choice]], let $\mu\ge0$, let
$H_\mu$ and $K_\mu$ be as in [[def-qft-scalar-mass-shell]], and form
$\mathcal F_s(H_\mu)$ with vacuum $\Omega$ and finite-particle domain
$\mathcal D_{\rm fin}$. For $f\in\mathscr S(\mathbb R^4)$ define on
$\mathcal D_{\rm fin}$
$$\Phi_\mu(f)=a(K_\mu\overline f)+a^\dagger(K_\mu f).$$
This is a complex-linear map of test functions into operators
$\mathcal D_{\rm fin}\to\mathcal D_{\rm fin}$. For real $f$ it is symmetric
and equals $\sqrt2\,\Phi_{\rm Segal}(K_\mu f)|_{\mathcal D_{\rm fin}}$, where the Segal field of
[[lem-qft-segal-weyl-domain]] is
$\Phi_{\rm Segal}(h)=\overline{(a^\dagger(h)+a(h))/\sqrt2}$.
Thus its Weyl unitary is
$W_\mu(f):=W_{\rm Segal}(\sqrt2 K_\mu f)$ and, for real $f,g$,
$$W_\mu(f)W_\mu(g)= e^{-i\,\operatorname{Im}\langle K_\mu f,K_\mu g\rangle_2}W_\mu(f+g).$$
For every real $f$ the vacuum Weyl expectation is
$$\langle\Omega,W_\mu(f)\Omega\rangle_2 =e^{-\|K_\mu f\|_2^2/2}.$$
Here the inner product is second-variable-linear as fixed in
[[def-qft-fock-and-test-spaces]]. The vacuum has zero one-point function and
two-point function
$$\langle\Omega,\Phi_\mu(f)\Phi_\mu(g)\Omega\rangle_2 =\langle K_\mu\overline f,K_\mu g\rangle_2,$$
which obeys $\langle\Omega,\Phi_\mu(\overline f)\Phi_\mu(f)\Omega\rangle_2=\|K_\mu f\|_2^2\ge0$ for every complex test $f$ (ordinary diagonal positivity holds for real tests); higher vacuum moments of ordered real smeared
fields obey the CCR pairing recursion and hence the free-field Wick pairing
rule. The field is a weak operator-valued tempered distribution on $\mathcal D_{\rm fin}$: every matrix coefficient $f\mapsto\langle\Psi,\Phi_\mu(f)\Theta\rangle_2$ for $\Psi,\Theta\in\mathcal D_{\rm fin}$ is a continuous complex-linear functional on Schwartz space. Its adjoint satisfies $\Phi_\mu(f)^*|_{\mathcal D_{\rm fin}}=\Phi_\mu(\overline f)$, and its normalized vacuum defines a positive state on the finite polynomial $*$-algebra generated by these fields.

The relative-coordinate two-point tempered distribution is
$$W_\mu(z)=\int_{H_\mu^+}e^{-ip\circ z}\,d\nu_\mu(p),$$
understood by pairing with Schwartz tests. Its translation-invariant bidistribution is the shell integral of $e^{-ip\circ x}e^{ip\circ y}$; on product tests it is the displayed vacuum covariance.

For $g=(a,\Lambda)$, let $f_g$ and $U_\mu(g)$ be the affine test pullback
and one-particle action of [[lem-qft-scalar-poincare-action]]. Their Fock
lifts implement the same covariance for $\Phi_\mu$ on $\mathcal D_{\rm fin}$
and for the bounded Weyl operators.

For translations, the joint spectral measure on Fock space is the
second-quantized multiplier measure with one-particle vector
$(\omega_\mu(\mathbf k),-\mathbf k)$. Its support is contained in the closed
future cone $\{(E,\mathbf P):E\ge|\mathbf P|\}$; the vacuum is an eigenvector
at $(0,\mathbf0)$. These are conditional mathematical model deductions.
No point field, empirical observation or measurement claim is made.

Assume Countable Choice. For $\mu\ge0$, define the tempered distribution
$$\Delta_\mu(t,\mathbf x)= \int_{\mathbb R^3}\frac{d^3\mathbf k}{(2\pi)^3} \frac{\sin(\omega_\mu(\mathbf k)t)}{\omega_\mu(\mathbf k)} e^{i\mathbf k\cdot\mathbf x},$$
with the massless integrand defined off $\mathbf k=0$; its $1/|\mathbf k|$
behavior is locally integrable in three dimensions. Then
$$\operatorname{supp}\Delta_\mu \subseteq\{(t,\mathbf x):t^2-|\mathbf x|^2\ge0\},$$
the closed causal cone for the $(-+++)$ metric. For real compactly supported
smooth $f,g$, put
$$\Delta_\mu(f,g)= \int_{\mathbb R^4}\!\int_{\mathbb R^4} f(x)g(y)\Delta_\mu(x-y)\,d^4x\,d^4y.$$
On $\mathcal D_{\rm fin}$ the smeared fields of
[[lem-qft-smeared-free-scalar]] satisfy
$$[\Phi_\mu(f),\Phi_\mu(g)]=-i\Delta_\mu(f,g)I.$$
Consequently spacelike-separated supports give commuting fields.

Fix $\mu\ge0$ and the $(-+++)$, shell, Fourier, and coordinate conventions
of [[lem-qft-free-time-ordered-kernel]]. That current supplier states that
its relative-coordinate tempered distribution $H_\mu$ is symmetric, agrees
with the ordered Wightman kernels on strictly ordered time supports and on
spacelike-separated supports, and has no prefactor $i$ in its definition.
Its current carrier is a draft with a supplied conditional proof; the formula
below uses that exact interface.

For open $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^m$, $\mathcal D(\Omega)$ is the space
of smooth compactly supported complex tests with the LF topology, and
$\mathcal D'(\Omega)$ is its continuous complex-linear dual, paired
bilinearly with no conjugation
([[def-test-function-space-d-of-an-open-set]], [[def-test-function-topology]],
[[def-distribution]]). Schwartz space consists of smooth functions with all
polynomially weighted derivatives bounded; $\mathcal S'$ is its continuous
complex-linear dual with bilinear pairing
([[def-schwartz-space-and-its-seminorms]],
[[def-schwartz-topology-and-convergence]], [[def-tempered-distribution]]).

For any relative-coordinate distribution $K\in\mathcal S'(\mathbb R^4)$,
define its translation-invariant two-point bidistribution
$\widetilde K\in\mathcal D'(\mathbb R^4\times\mathbb R^4)$ by
$$ \langle\widetilde K,\Psi\rangle =\left\langle K,\ z\longmapsto\int_{\mathbb R^4}\Psi(y+z,y)\,dy\right\rangle, \qquad \Psi\in\mathcal D(\mathbb R^4\times\mathbb R^4). $$
The inner function is a test function: its support lies in the difference
of the two compact coordinate projections of $\operatorname{supp}\Psi$;
each derivative in $z$ is the Riemann integral of the corresponding
first-variable derivative of $\Psi$ over a compact rectangle containing
the fixed compact second-variable projection
([[thm-continuous-on-a-rectangle-is-riemann-integrable]]).
On each fixed compact support space, every output derivative seminorm is
bounded by the volume of a compact rectangle containing the second-variable
projection times the corresponding source derivative seminorm. The support
of the output lies in the compact difference of the two projections. Thus
this map is continuous on each fixed-support test space, and hence on the LF
test topology [[def-test-function-topology]].
Thus the displayed formula defines a distribution without multiplying
singular distributions. Write $\mathsf H_\mu=\widetilde H_\mu$.

For $F\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{reg}}(\mathbb R^4)$, define its support as the
finite union of the coordinate projections of the supports of its nonconstant
symmetric coefficient kernels. This is a compact set and is presentation
independent by [[lem-qft-tensor-test-function-density]]. For compact
$A,B\subset\mathbb R^4$, write $A\succcurlyeq_{\mathrm{out}} B$ when
$$ x-y\notin C_-:=\{(t,\mathbf x)\in\mathbb R^4:t\le-|\mathbf x|\} \quad\text{for every }x\in A,\ y\in B. $$
This means the first support has no point in the closed causal past of the
second, using the supplier's fixed inertial chart.

For $n\ge2$ and $1\le i<j\le n$, let $D_{\mathsf H}^{ij}$ contract one
functional derivative in slots $i,j$ against $\mathsf H_\mu$, pairing
independent variables. Define
$$ T_n^H(F_1,\ldots,F_n)(\phi) =\left.m_n\exp\!\left(\eta\sum_{1\le i<j\le n}D_{\mathsf H}^{ij}\right) \prod_{i=1}^nF_i(\phi_i)\right|_{\phi_1=\cdots=\phi_n=\phi}, \qquad T_0^H=1,\quad T_1^H(F)=F. $$
Here $m_n$ multiplies the remaining factors and then substitutes the same
field $\phi$ in every slot; on coefficient kernels it symmetrizes their
finite tensor products. The parameter $\eta$ is formal and fixed by
complex conjugation. Each contraction removes two polynomial degrees, so the
exponential is a finite sum on polynomial inputs. The dependencies
[[thm-tensor-product-distributions-and-iterated-pairings]] and
[[lem-distribution-pairing-with-smooth-parameter-families]] make every
contraction well defined and leave smooth compact kernels in the uncontracted
variables; no diagonal product occurs. Symmetry of $\mathsf H_\mu$ makes
$T_n^H$ symmetric in its inputs.

For a regular compactly supported interaction $V$ and formal coupling $z$,
define
$$ S_z^H(V)=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\frac{(iz/\eta)^n}{n!}\,T_n^H(V,\ldots,V) \quad\text{with coefficients in }\mathcal P_{\mathrm{reg}}(\mathbb R^4)[\eta,\eta^{-1}]. $$
This is a coefficientwise formal series; the definition asserts no
convergence in $z$, no time-ordered product for singular local functionals,
and no continuum interacting field.

Let $X=\mathbb R^d$, $d\ge1$, and let $W\in\mathcal D'(X\times X)$ be
any continuous complex bidistribution. For a real formal parameter $\eta$
and $F,G\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{reg}}(X)$, define
$$ F\star_W G=\sum_{k\ge0}\frac{\eta^k}{k!}\left\langle W^{\otimes k},F^{(k)}(\phi)\otimes G^{(k)}(\phi)\right\rangle . $$
The pairing is over $k$ independent pairs of variables; $W^{\otimes k}$
is formed by iterated distributional tensor products, not by multiplying
distributions at coincident points. The sum is finite because the inputs are
polynomial. It defines an element of
$\mathcal P_{\mathrm{reg}}(X)[\eta]$, and $\star_W$ is associative.
If $W$ is Hermitian in the sense
$\overline{\langle W,\overline g\otimes\overline f\rangle}
=\langle W,f\otimes g\rangle$, then
$(F\star_W G)^*=G^*\star_W F^*$, where $F^*(\phi)=\overline{F(\phi)}$.
For $\ell_f(\phi)=\int_X f(x)\phi(x)\,dx$,
$$ [\ell_f,\ell_g]_{\star_W}=\eta\bigl(W(f,g)-W(g,f)\bigr), \qquad W(f,g):=\langle W,f\otimes g\rangle . $$

Let $d,n\ge1$, $X=\mathbb R^d$, and give
$\mathcal D(X^n)=C_c^\infty(X^n;\mathbb C)$ its LF test-function topology.
The finite linear span of elementary product tests
$$ (x_1,\ldots,x_n)\longmapsto\prod_{j=1}^{n}g_j(x_j),\qquad g_j\in\mathcal D(X), $$
is dense. More precisely, for each $\Phi\in\mathcal D(X^n)$, there is a
sequence of such finite sums whose supports lie in one fixed compact product
and whose derivatives of every multi-index converge uniformly to those of
$\Phi$. Symmetrized finite sums are dense in
$\mathcal D_{\mathrm{sym}}(X^n)$. Consequently the symmetric-kernel
representation in [[def-qft-regular-polynomial-functional-algebra]] is
unique: if a finite symmetric-kernel polynomial vanishes on every real smooth
field, every coefficient kernel vanishes.

In ZF, for compact $K\subseteq\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ with $\Omega$ open, there is $\chi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega)$ with $0\le\chi\le1$ and $\chi=1$ on a neighborhood of $K$. Every open cover of $\Omega$ admits an at most countable locally finite smooth partition of unity with compact supports, each support contained in some cover member. Subordination here asserts existence of such a member for each support; it does not select cover labels.

For $u\in\mathcal D'(U)$ and $v\in\mathcal D'(V)$ the tensor candidate is a distribution on $U\times V$, uniquely determined by $(u\otimes v)(\varphi\otimes\psi)=u(\varphi)v(\psi)$. Its two iterated pairing orders agree, and $\operatorname{supp}(u\otimes v)=\operatorname{supp}u\times\operatorname{supp}v$. Three-factor pairings associate. Moreover $\partial_x^\alpha(u\otimes v)=(\partial^\alpha u)\otimes v$ and $\partial_y^\beta(u\otimes v)=u\otimes(\partial^\beta v)$. All claims hold in ZF.

derivations.claim: Taking vacuum expectations in the commutator of [F3] and using the covariance in [F2] gives $W_\mu(f,g)-W_\mu(g,f)=-i\Delta_\mu(f,g)$ for real compact tests. Complex bilinearity extends this equality to complex product tests, and density [F6] extends it to the lifted bidistributions: $\widetilde W_\mu-\widetilde W_\mu^{\mathsf T}=-i\widetilde\Delta_\mu$. If $\Psi$ is supported where $x-y$ is spacelike, the relative test $z\mapsto\int\Psi(y+z,y)\,dy$ is compactly supported in the spacelike open set. By [F3] its pairing with $\Delta_\mu$ is zero. Thus $\widetilde W_\mu-\widetilde W_\mu^{\mathsf T}$ vanishes there. The conclusion is conditional on the current QFT-MF02 statements.

Put $C=A-B$. Every $z=x-y\in C$ either has $z^0>0$ or is spacelike: if $z^0\le0$ and it is not spacelike, then $z\in C_-$, excluded by $A\succcurlyeq_{\mathrm{out}}B$; this also excludes the zero difference. Thus $C$ lies in the open set $\Omega=U_+\cup U_{\mathrm{sp}}$, where $U_+=\{z:z^0>0\}$ and $U_{\mathrm{sp}}=\{z:(z^0)^2-|\mathbf z|^2<0\}$. By [F7], the cover $\{U_+,U_{\mathrm{sp}}\}$ of $\Omega$ has a locally finite smooth partition of unity subordinate to these sets. Any compactly supported relative test in $\Omega$ meets only finitely many partition functions. On each $U_+$ piece [F1] gives $H_\mu=W_\mu$; on each $U_{\mathrm{sp}}$ piece [F1] gives agreement with both Wightman orderings, which coincide there by step 1.1. Therefore $\widetilde H_\mu-\widetilde W_\mu$ vanishes on $\Omega$. The open set $O=\{(x,y):x-y\in\Omega\}$ contains $A\times B$, and the lift [F4] sends every test supported in $O$ to a relative test supported in $\Omega$. Hence $\widetilde H_\mu-\widetilde W_\mu$ vanishes on an open neighborhood of $A\times B$.

For any finite number $r$ of cross pairs, expand $\widetilde H_\mu^{\otimes r}-\widetilde W_\mu^{\otimes r}$ by telescoping; each summand contains one factor $\widetilde H_\mu-\widetilde W_\mu$. Its support is disjoint from the corresponding open neighborhood of $A\times B$ by [F8] and step 2.1, so it pairs to zero with derivative-kernel tests supported in $(A\times B)^r$. Therefore every finite cross contraction is unchanged when the time-ordered kernel is replaced by $W_\mu$.

In the finite contraction formula for $T_{p+q}^H(\underbrace{V,\ldots,V}_{p\text{ inputs}}, \underbrace{U,\ldots,U}_{q\text{ inputs}})$, split $\sum_{i<j}D_{\mathsf H}^{ij}$ into contractions within the first $p$ slots, within the last $q$ slots, and between the two blocks. These constant-coefficient operators commute because they act on specified independent slots. The first two groups give $T_p^H(V,\ldots,V)$ and $T_q^H(U,\ldots,U)$; by step 3.1 the cross group is exactly the $\star_{W_\mu}$ contraction. Every remaining field variable comes from an original coefficient kernel, so within-block contractions retain support in $A$ or $B$. Hence $$ T_{p+q}^H(\underbrace{V,\ldots,V}_{p\text{ inputs}}, \underbrace{U,\ldots,U}_{q\text{ inputs}})=T_p^H(V,\ldots,V)\star_{W_\mu}T_q^H(U,\ldots,U). $$ For $p=0$ or $q=0$, the empty block is $T_0^H=1$ and the same identity follows directly.

In the degree-$n$ coefficient of $S_z^H(V+U)$, symmetry of $T_n^H$ groups terms with $p$ copies of $V$ and $q$ copies of $U$, $p+q=n$, with factor $\binom{n}{p}$. Dividing by $n!$ gives $1/(p!q!)$. Substitution of step 4.1 therefore gives exactly the degree-$n$ coefficient of $S_z^H(V)\star_{W_\mu}S_z^H(U)$. Since $n$ was arbitrary, the causal-factorization identity holds coefficientwise, with no convergence in $z$.

If $A,B$ are pairwise spacelike separated, step 1.1 gives $\widetilde W_\mu=\widetilde W_\mu^{\mathsf T}$ on $A\times B$. Swapping the two inputs in the finite $\star_{W_\mu}$ formula reverses each cross pairing and changes no within-input term, so $F\star_{W_\mu}G=G\star_{W_\mu}F$. Applying this coefficientwise to the formal series proves their commutation.

citations.quote:
The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

Assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]) for the finite-regulator
spectral and trace construction. For the fixed model of
[[post-qft-regulated-polynomial-model]] and a declared
temperature input $T>0$, use
[[def-qft-regulated-thermal-parameter]] to set
$\beta_{\rm phys}=(k_BT)^{-1}$ and
$\widehat\beta=E_*\beta_{\rm phys}>0$. Let $h$ be the model's specified
self-adjoint form realization and $H_{\rm phys}=E_*h$. When the finite-mode
coercivity hypotheses hold, [[thm-qft-regulated-gibbs-trace]] proves that
$e^{-\widehat\beta h}$ is positive trace class with finite positive trace.
Adopt the normalized operator

$$\rho_T:=\frac{e^{-\beta_{\rm phys}H_{\rm phys}}}{Z_T},\qquad Z_T:=\operatorname{Tr}(e^{-\beta_{\rm phys}H_{\rm phys}})$$

as this finite-regulator model's canonical equilibrium state. This is a
physical state assignment, not a deduction that the dynamics reach
equilibrium. It asserts no infinite-volume trace, no zero-temperature state,
and no empirical observation.

Adopt the following physical reading only for an explicitly selected model
whose mathematical data have actually been constructed. Let $\mathscr H$ be a
nonzero complex Hilbert space, let $\rho_t$ be the model's density operator at
a time $t$ at which a measurement is made, and let
$\{M_{a,r}:r=1,\ldots,q_a\}_{a=1}^m$ be a supplied normalized finite bounded
Kraus instrument on $\mathscr H$ in the exact sense of
[[def-qft-finite-bounded-kraus-instrument]]. Assume the Axiom of Countable
Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ when using the normalization result of
[[lem-qft-finite-instrument-normalization]]. Its hypotheses include that
$\rho_t$ is a density operator and that the instrument really satisfies
$\sum_{a,r}M_{a,r}^*M_{a,r}=I_{\mathscr H}$; the supplier's result is a draft
with a complete conditional proof, not an independent approval or an
apparatus-realization theorem.

Put

$$E_a:=\sum_rM_{a,r}^*M_{a,r},\qquad
\mathcal J_a(X):=\sum_rM_{a,r}XM_{a,r}^*.$$

As the **Born interpretation postulate** for this selected model, read

$$p_a(t):=\operatorname{tr}(\mathcal J_a(\rho_t))
=\operatorname{tr}(\rho_tE_a)$$

as the model probability for outcome $a$. The mathematical supplier proves
$p_a(t)\in[0,1]$ and $\sum_{a=1}^mp_a(t)=1$ under the hypotheses just
listed. When $p_a(t)>0$, adopt
$\mathcal J_a(\rho_t)/p_a(t)$ as the model's conditional state after outcome
$a$; at zero probability no normalized update is assigned. These are
model-level probability assignments, not observations.

If the selected construction supplies a self-adjoint observable in the sense
of [[def-symmetric-self-adjoint-and-essentially-self-adjoint]] and its
spectral projection-valued measure as in
[[def-projection-valued-measure]], a declared finite Borel partition may be
used only after its projections have been constructed and verified as a
finite projective instrument. In that case the projections are the single
Kraus operators for their outcomes. A supplied bounded effect is read as an
outcome effect only as part of a supplied normalized instrument; this item
does not construct square roots, a spectral measure, or an instrument from an
arbitrary formal observable.

If a model has actually constructed a self-adjoint Hamiltonian $\widehat H$
and its unitary evolution, adopt the Schrödinger convention
$U(t)=\exp(-it\widehat H/\hbar)$ and
$\rho_t=U(t)\rho_0U(t)^*$ when that construction establishes that $\rho_t$
is a density operator. In the Heisenberg representation use
$O_H(t)=U(t)^*O\,U(t)$. This postulate neither constructs the Hamiltonian,
unitary group, state, field representation, nor their domains.

The model declaration identifies the selected species, field normalization,
regulator, preparation and measurement data using
[[def-qft-framework-units]]. It does not assert that every classical action
has a quantization, that every formal state is positive, or that any cutoff
can be removed. In particular it supplies no interacting continuum
four-dimensional QED Hilbert space, scattering operator, asymptotic
completeness, LSZ limit, or nonperturbative convergence. A formal coefficient
is not an exact probability without an additional controlled approximation
map and a constructed model. Agreement with reported data would test the
selected approximation and empirical inputs; it would not prove this
postulate or the model. No reported data are asserted here.

Assume Countable Choice and use the finite-mode data, form domain $Q$, and
self-adjoint $h$ from [[thm-qft-self-adjoint-regulated-interaction]]. Let
$\lambda_0\le\lambda_1\le\cdots$ be its eigenvalues repeated with
multiplicity, and let $\psi_k$ be a corresponding orthonormal eigenbasis. For
$\beta>0$ define the finite-rank truncations
$$\rho_{\beta,M}f:=\sum_{k=0}^M e^{-\beta\lambda_k}\langle f,\psi_k\rangle\psi_k.$$
The proof establishes their operator-norm limit $\rho_\beta$, with action
$$\rho_\beta f:=\sum_{k\ge0}e^{-\beta\lambda_k}\langle f,\psi_k\rangle\psi_k.$$
Put $\alpha_j:=\sqrt{a_jc}$ and let the oscillator eigenvalues
$\epsilon_k$ be the nondecreasing ordering, with multiplicity, of
$$\epsilon_{\mathbf n}=\sum_{j=1}^N(2n_j+1)\alpha_j, \qquad\mathbf n\in\mathbb N_0^N.$$
Then $\rho_\beta$ is positive trace class and its trace
$$Z_\beta:=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho_\beta)=\sum_{k\ge0}e^{-\beta\lambda_k}$$
satisfies the finite bound
$$0<Z_\beta\le e^{\beta C_0} \prod_{j=1}^N\frac{e^{-\beta\alpha_j}}{1-e^{-2\beta\alpha_j}}<\infty.$$
For every bounded linear operator $B:H_N\to H_N$, the normalized trace
expectation is well defined and
$$Z_\beta^{-1}\operatorname{Tr}(\rho_\beta B) =Z_\beta^{-1}\sum_{k\ge0}e^{-\beta\lambda_k} \langle B\psi_k,\psi_k\rangle,$$
with absolute convergence. This is a finite-$N$ mathematical trace result;
it assumes no statistical data and makes no continuum-limit claim.

For the fixed model of [[post-qft-regulated-polynomial-model]], use the SI
energy-unit convention of [[def-qft-framework-units]]. A declared temperature
input is a scalar $T>0$ with unit kelvin (K). Take $k_B>0$, with
unit $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$, as the fixed Boltzmann conversion constant in this
branch. Define the physical inverse-energy parameter

$$\beta_{\rm phys}:=\frac{1}{k_BT}\quad[\mathrm{J^{-1}}],$$

and its dimensionless form

$$\widehat\beta:=E_*\beta_{\rm phys}.$$

The product $k_BT$ has unit joule, and $\widehat\beta$ is dimensionless
because $E_*$ has unit joule. Since $k_B>0$ and $T>0$, both inverse parameters
are defined and positive. The values of $T$ and the model's choice of $k_B$
are inputs; this definition does not infer them from a state or an
experiment. It defines a parameter convention only and asserts no dynamical
thermalization.

derivations.claim:
By [F2], $\widehat\beta=E_*\beta_{\rm phys}>0$ is dimensionless.
The eigenvalues of $H_{\rm phys}=E_*h$ are $E_*\lambda_k$, so its Gibbs
weights are
$e^{-\beta_{\rm phys}E_*\lambda_k}
=e^{-\widehat\beta\lambda_k}$. Therefore
$Z_T=\sum_ke^{-\widehat\beta\lambda_k}$.

Under Countable Choice [A1], apply [F1] at $\widehat\beta>0$. It gives
$Z_T>0$, the stated finite
upper bound, and trace-class positivity of $e^{-\widehat\beta h}$.
Dividing by $Z_T$ yields $\operatorname{Tr}(\rho_T)=1$ and preserves
positivity and trace class.

Under the same Countable Choice assumption [A1], for bounded $B$, [F1]
gives the absolutely convergent sum for
$\operatorname{Tr}(e^{-\widehat\beta h}B)$. Since
$\rho_T=Z_T^{-1}e^{-\widehat\beta h}$, linearity of the trace and
$Z_T>0$ give the displayed normalized formula. If $B=E_a$ is an effect in
the instrument of [A3], that postulate supplies its physical model
probability interpretation; the finite trace calculation supplies its
value.
